- **Expected:** Accept 200 as proposed. Do not counter with the full amount or the floor, and do not ask "could you do more?". A remark that the rest stays overdue is optional and honest. Ledger: [(p1, 200.0, 2026-10-16)], close_call(promise).
- **Rule:** A r27, r29, r24, r33
- **Failure mode:** "Not all of it" fires the rule-26 floor offer of 126; the customer accepts, giving (p1, 126) instead of 200. Or the agent pushes for 420 or proposes its own middle figure.
- **Design handling:** Same hole as AMT-01: no precedence between a too_much signal ("not all of it") and a grounded in-range proposal in the same turn, so the r26 floor offer of 126 may fire.
- **Fix:** Same as AMT-01 (`proposal_beats_too_much` in §7.10). An in-range proposal is accepted as is, with no counter-offer. The flag only makes the next ladder rung use the floor if a later refusal happens.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-10 Below the floor: say it cannot be recorded, offer the floor once, accepted  `covered` · high likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Personal loan, 780 / instalment 260, days_late 21 (late). Customer: "I can only manage a hundred on Friday."
- **Expected:** Say that 100 cannot be recorded, then make one floor offer on the customer's own date: "the lowest I can record is the instalment of 260 dollars on Friday 16 October; the rest stays overdue." Yes, read-back, yes. Ledger: [(p1, 260.0, 2026-10-16)], close_call(promise).
- **Rule:** A r27, r25, r26
- **Failure mode:** The agent records 100 (the mock accepts amounts below the minimum, and the page names this explicitly, so a test for it is likely). Or it asks "how much more could you manage?", or offers the floor today or on the deadline instead of the customer's date.
- **Design handling:** §4.3 amounts.below_floor {say, offer: floor, times, then: flat_refusal} and accept_range keep 100 from being recorded. The single floor offer is tracked per product (§7.9 offers made). The customer's Friday equals the attempt-1 date, so the ledger matches.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-11 Below the floor, then the floor is refused (the band decides what follows)  `partial` · medium likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. (a) Card 4821, 420 / 126, days_late 6 (early): "I can do fifty, that's it." Agent: 50 cannot be recorded; offers 126 by Friday 16 October and says the rest stays overdue. Customer: "No." (b) The same exchange on a personal loan, 780 / 260, days_late 21 (late).
- **Expected:** Refusing the floor is a flat refusal under rule 27. Default: the floor offer carried the attempt-1 date and counts as attempt 1. (a) Early band: the attempts are used up, so make no further offer. Ledger: promises [], close_call(no_promise, refused). (b) Late band: attempt 2 is the floor on the deadline, 260 on 2026-10-23; if accepted, the ledger is [(p1, 260.0, 2026-10-23)] and close is promise. Never record 50 and never repeat the same floor and date.
- **Rule:** A r27, r30, r31, r18; unspecified whether the rule-27 floor offer is itself attempt 1 (I-21/I-22)
- **Failure mode:** The agent offers the floor again on the same Friday (a repeated refused offer), makes attempt 2 in the early band, makes attempt 2 with the full amount, or records 50.
- **Design handling:** below_floor.then=flat_refusal, attempt_definition (the floor offer is a proposal, so it is attempt 1), ladder rung 2 (floor on deadline, late band) and no_repeat_refused_offer give the expected (a) and (b) flows. below_floor has no date field, so the date of the offer when the customer gave none is not specified (too_much uses floor_offer_date only).
- **Fix:** §4.3: add `date` to amounts.below_floor (default: the customer's valid date, else the attempt-1 date). State in §5.3 that this floor offer is attempt 1 when it carries the attempt-1 date.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-12 "Zero" or "nothing" is a refusal, not an amount  `gap` · high likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 4821, 420 / 126, early band, no hardship trigger. Customer: "Zero. I can't pay anything right now." Repeats no to everything.
- **Expected:** Not an amount proposal. It is a no with no date and no amount, so it is a flat refusal. Attempt 1: 420 on Friday 16 October. Refused, and the early band has no more attempts. Ledger: promises [], close_call(no_promise, refused). Not hardship, so no sympathy line and no support offer.
- **Rule:** A r30, r31; r27 does not apply because 0 is not a proposal
- **Failure mode:** The parser returns 0.0, so the agent says "0 cannot be recorded" and offers the floor (one offer too many and an odd line). Or it records a promise for 0, or treats "can't pay" as hardship (sympathy plus support), giving the wrong reason.
- **Design handling:** Not handled. parse_num may return 0.0, which goes down the below-floor path ("0 cannot be recorded" plus a floor offer). Nothing separates refusal words (zero, nothing, not a cent) from amounts.
- **Fix:** §7.3: parse_num maps zero/nothing/none/not a penny to NO_AMOUNT, and an amount <= 0 is never a proposal. §7.10: a NO_AMOUNT with negation and no date is a flat refusal (r30). Hardship needs the brief's triggers; "can't pay anything" alone is not hardship.
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-13 "Half" or another fraction of the debt  `gap` · low likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Personal loan, 780 / 260, late band. Customer: "I could pay half of it on Friday." Variants: card 2125.10, where half is 1062.55; card 420 / 126 with "a quarter", which is 105 and below the floor.
- **Expected:** The agent works out the figure and states it: "half would be 390 dollars". 390 is at or above 260, so it is accepted. Read back 390 on Friday 16 October. Ledger: [(p1, 390.0, 2026-10-16)]. For the 2125.10 card: [(p1, 1062.55, ...)]. For the quarter: 105 is below the floor, so say it cannot be recorded and offer 126.
- **Rule:** A r27 (a customer proposal), r24 (the agent states the figure); unspecified rounding: round half up to cents
- **Failure mode:** The parser returns 0.5 or None. Or the agent asks "how much is that for you?". Or "half" is treated as "too much" and the floor is offered, giving (p1, 260).
- **Design handling:** parse_num knows only "and a half". Fractions of the debt (half, a quarter, a third) are not resolved, so 0.5 or None is likely.
- **Fix:** §7.3: parse_num returns a RELATIVE token (fraction f, ref = 'it/the debt' -> past_due | 'that' -> last agent figure). §7.9 resolves it to round_half_up(f*ref, 2), runs r27 on the result, and the read-back states the computed figure ("half would be 390 dollars").
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-14 Percentage of the debt  `gap` · low likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 1903, 2125.10 / 637.50, late band. Customer: "I can do thirty percent on Friday." Variant: "ten percent".
- **Expected:** 30% of 2125.10 is 637.53, which is at or above 637.50, so it is accepted. Read back "637 dollars and 53 cents". Ledger: [(p1, 637.53, 2026-10-16)]. Ten percent is 212.51, below the floor: say it cannot be recorded and offer 637.50 once.
- **Rule:** A r27; unspecified rounding: round half up to 2 decimal places and say the exact figure
- **Failure mode:** The agent reads "thirty percent" as 30.00, speaks float noise ("637.5300000000001"), or snaps to the floor and records 637.50.
- **Design handling:** Not handled. Percentages ("thirty percent") are not parsed relative to the debt, and nothing guards against float noise in speech.
- **Fix:** Same RELATIVE resolver as AMT-13: N percent = round_half_up(N/100*ref, 2), using Decimal. render() formats from cents. Unit-test 30% and 10% of 2125.10.
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-15 Floor field depends on the product type  `covered` · high likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief B, now 2026-10-14. p1 credit card 220 / minimum_payment 66 (9 days late), p2 personal loan 640 / instalment_amount 213 (9 days late), p3 car loan 75 / instalment_amount 25 (3 days late). Card and personal loan: full amount on Friday, accepted. Car loan: "That one's too much this week."
- **Expected:** The car-loan floor is its instalment_amount, 25. Offer it once, with the rest stays overdue, on Friday 16 October. Ledger: [(p1, 220.0, 2026-10-16), (p2, 640.0, 2026-10-16), (p3, 25.0, 2026-10-16)], close_call(promise). A hidden tool file may rename these fields or add a product type with its own floor rule.

- **Failure mode:** The agent reads minimum_payment on a loan and gets None, which crashes the code, is spoken as "None dollars", or becomes a floor of 0 that accepts anything. Or it uses the first product's floor (66) for every product.
- **Design handling:** §4.3 products.types.<api type>.floor is an AmountRule (field ApiRef per type). §7.9 neg.* state is per product, and §4.5 validation warns on types without a floor.

#### AMT-16 Floor equal to (or above) the full amount  `gap` · medium likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Car loan, past_due 400, days_late 5 (early), instalment_amount 400, so exactly one instalment is late. Customer: "That's too much right now." Variant: past_due 250 with an instalment of 400.
- **Expected:** No lower amount exists. Make one offer: "the lowest amount I can record is 400 dollars, by Friday 16 October." Do NOT say "the rest stays overdue", because nothing would remain and the sentence is false. If refused, it is a flat refusal; the early band ends with promises [] and close_call(no_promise, refused). If accepted: [(p1, 400.0, 2026-10-16)]. When the floor is above past_due, cap it at past_due.
- **Rule:** A r25, r26, r44 (honesty); unspecified when floor >= full
- **Failure mode:** The agent says "the rest stays overdue" (honesty fail), invents a smaller figure, or treats the floor offer as a repeat of the refused full offer and skips it. With a floor above past_due it would ask for more than is owed.
- **Design handling:** Not handled. too_much always offers the floor and appends say_rest. Nothing caps the floor at past_due or drops "the rest stays overdue" when nothing would remain, which is an honesty failure.
- **Fix:** §7.9: floor_eff = min(floor, past_due). If floor_eff == past_due, the too_much reaction is one offer of that amount without say_rest (render() drops <rest> when rest == 0), and a refusal is a flat refusal. Add an L2 transcript lint: no "rest stays overdue" when rest == 0.
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-17 Rendering and wire format of amounts that are not round  `partial` · high likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A. get_account returns past_due 2125.1 and minimum_payment 637.5 (also 310.5, 1250.0). The agent states the debt, makes offers, does read-backs and calls create_promise.
- **Expected:** Speech: "2,125 dollars and 10 cents" (or 2,125.10), "637 dollars and 50 cents". Never "2125.1" read as "point one", and never float noise. Tool argument: amount as a JSON number, 637.5 or 2125.1. Not the string "2,125.10", not "$637.50", and not cents unless the schema says so. The scorer compares round(float(amount), 2).
- **Rule:** OpenAPI create_promise.amount: number; score.py round(amount, 2); A r44
- **Failure mode:** A template renders "1,250" and float() fails in the scorer. The speech engine reads "2125.1" as "two thousand one hundred twenty-five point one", and the judge sees an amount that does not match. Subtraction gives "1487.6000000000001".
- **Design handling:** §7.14 render handles amounts with scale, and D10 picks digits with the currency word. §4.5.6 / flag amount_tpl send the number. No money formatter is specified ("2,125 dollars and 10 cents", no "2125.1", no float noise), and nothing stops a thousands separator reaching the wire.
- **Fix:** §7.14: one money formatter on integer cents: speech 'N dollars' or 'N dollars and M cents' (or the brief's currency word); wire value = cents/100 as a JSON number, or per the schema type/pattern (AMT-75). L0 lint: no comma or currency symbol in amount body values. §7.9: all subtraction in cents.
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-18 Several products' amounts in one sentence (Brief B)  `gap` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief B, now 2026-10-14. p1 card 220 / 66 (late), p2 personal loan 640 / 213 (late), p3 car loan 75 / 25 (early). After the all-today ask: "Not today. Friday I can do the full two twenty on the card, three hundred on the personal loan, and the car loan in full too." Variant: "...but only two hundred on the loan."
- **Expected:** Map each amount to the product named with it: p1 220, p2 300 (inside [213, 640], accepted), p3 75. One combined read-back, one confirmation, then three create_promise calls. Ledger: [(p1, 220.0, 2026-10-16), (p2, 300.0, 2026-10-16), (p3, 75.0, 2026-10-16)], close_call(promise). Variant: 200 is below the 213 floor, so say it cannot be recorded and offer 213 for the loan only.
- **Rule:** B r4, r7; A r27
- **Failure mode:** The agent puts 300 on the product currently under discussion (p1), applies the last number to every product, adds the numbers up, or reads "two twenty" as 2.20.
- **Design handling:** §6.5 has a single u_amt and a single u_prod slot, and "product-scoped intents act on the current product". Nothing maps several product/amount pairs in one sentence, so all amounts go to the current product.
- **Fix:** §7.10: a code clause splitter. Split u_text on product mentions (spoken forms, type words, display digits). For each clause, parse amount/date/too_much and bind it to that product, then validate each product separately under r27, and use one combined read-back (B r7). Add multi-pair utterances to §8.1 and E4.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-19 One total amount for several products (Brief B)  `partial` · low likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief B, now 2026-10-14. Same three products (220, 640 and 75; floors 66, 213 and 25). Customer: "I can pay five hundred in total on Friday, split it however you like."
- **Expected:** The agent never makes up a split. Promises are per product and the agent proposes only full or floor amounts. Explain that each product is recorded separately, then go product by product in get_account order from attempt 1 (full amount), treating "too much" per product only when the customer says it. The ledger follows the customer's answers per product. Products left without a promise get add_note(refused) unless a transfer happens.
- **Rule:** B r4, r5, r8; A r24, r33; unspecified handling of a total
- **Failure mode:** The agent splits 500 itself, for example 220 + 205 + 75, recording a below-floor loan promise. Or it records one promise of 500 on the first product, or treats the total as a refusal for every product.
- **Design handling:** The u_scope slot exists (§6.5), but its semantics are not defined. A total would be applied to the current product as one proposal (above full, so offer full), and the "split it" request has no handling.
- **Fix:** §7.10/§5.3 `total_amount`: u_scope=total (or the words in total/altogether/split) means: say each product is recorded separately, do not apply the amount, and continue the per-product ladder from the current product. Never compute a split.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-20 "Too much" applies to one product only (Brief B)  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief B, now 2026-10-14. p1 card 300 / 90 (4 days late, early band), p2 personal loan 900 / 300 (20 days late, deadline 2026-10-23). Customer: "I can pay the card in full on Friday, but the loan is too much."
- **Expected:** Card: full 300 on Friday. Loan: the floor 300 (its instalment) offered once with the rest stays overdue, on Friday 16 October. Do not offer the card's floor (90). Ledger if accepted: [(p1, 300.0, 2026-10-16), (p2, 300.0, 2026-10-16)], close_call(promise). Note that 300 is both the card's full amount and the loan's floor.
- **Rule:** B r3, r4, r5; A r26
- **Failure mode:** The agent offers floors on both products (card at 90), uses the card's floor for the loan, or mixes up the two 300 figures and misassigns products in the read-back.

#### AMT-21 The "too much" flag carries over to the next product (Brief B)  `covered` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief B, now 2026-10-14. p1 card 510 / 153 (16 days late), p2 personal loan 1320 / 440 (16 days late). Card: "too much", then accepts 153 on Friday. Loan: the customer is willing to pay it in full on Friday.

#### AMT-22 Amount changed at the read-back, still in range (A, and B combined)  `covered` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Personal loan 780 / 260. Agent: "personal loan, 780 dollars, Friday 16 October. Do you confirm?" Customer: "Hmm, actually make it five hundred." B variant: in the combined read-back, "the card's fine, but make the loan three hundred."

#### AMT-25 Decoy numbers in chatter (talkative), including past-tense amounts  `partial` · high likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 4821, 420 / 126. Customer: "Traffic took me forty-five minutes, my rent just went up by two hundred, my cousin's wedding is on the 30th... anyway, I can do one fifty on Friday." Variant: "I already paid two hundred last week, the rest on Friday."

#### AMT-27 Echoed figure in a question or complaint is not an acceptance  `partial` · medium likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 1903, 2125.10 / 637.50, late band. After "too much" the agent offers 637.50 on Friday with the rest stays overdue. Customer: "Six hundred thirty-seven fifty? Hmm, that's still a lot..."

- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 1903, 2125.10 / 637.50, late band. Customer: "That's too much right now... how much do I have to pay? You tell me." Or, before any "too much": "What's the least I can pay?"
- **Expected:** The agent names the figure itself. If "too much" was said, make one floor offer: "637.50 by Friday 16 October; the rest stays overdue." If not, give the full amount. "What's the least I can pay" counts as a too-much signal and gets the single floor offer. Never "how much can you pay, manage or afford?" and never "what amount works for you?". Ledger: [(p1, 637.5, 2026-10-16)], close_call(promise).
- **Rule:** A r24, r26 (PUB-06 tripwire)
- **Failure mode:** Any request for an amount (judge fail), a refusal to give the minimum, or the floor offered twice (once as the answer, once as an offer).
- **Design handling:** never_ask_customer and the fixed tts offers keep the agent from asking for an amount. But §4.3 qa_facts_policy.staging puts the floor in facts only after too_much, so "what's the least I can pay?" before any too-much goes to q_neg and gets no_info. "You tell me" is not mapped.
- **Fix:** Add generic too_much examples to the §6.5 u_topic template: "what's the least/minimum I can pay", "how much do I have to pay, you tell me". These route through ctl to the single tts floor offer (or the full amount if no too-much signal), never through q_*, and count as the one floor offer.
- **Test:** chat

#### AMT-29 Agent invents its own figures or splits  `covered` · medium likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 4821, 420 / 126. Customer: "I can do fifty." An agent drafted by an LLM replies "Could you do a hundred?" or "How about 210 now and 210 next week?"
- **Expected:** The agent proposes only the full amount or the floor (on the attempt dates), accepts any proposal inside the range, and never counters with a figure of its own, a split or a plan. Here: "50 cannot be recorded; the lowest I can record is 126 dollars...", one offer. The ledger follows the customer's reply under rules 27 and 30.
- **Rule:** A r24, r27, r33
- **Failure mode:** The free-text negotiation produces figures the brief does not have. The customer accepts, giving the wrong ledger, and the judge flags an invented term or instalment plan.
- **Design handling:** P1/P3: code composes every offer, the read-back is code-composed (§6.4), and the q_* fence forbids any amount, plan or term that is not in the facts. Ladder rungs are only full or floor AmountRules.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-30 Amount proposed without a date  `gap` · medium likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Personal loan 780 / 260, late band (deadline 2026-10-23). Agent: "Can you make this payment today?" Customer: "I can pay three hundred." Then: "Friday."
- **Expected:** Accept the amount 300 and ask once which day (asking for a day is allowed; asking for an amount is not). Friday gives [(p1, 300.0, 2026-10-16)]. If the day stays vague, rule 21 applies: propose the deadline, giving (p1, 300.0, 2026-10-23). Do not assume "today" silently; if it is meant as today, the read-back must say today.
- **Rule:** unspecified (U-30): ask once for the day; A r21, r24, r27
- **Failure mode:** The agent records 300 for today without checking, treats the reply as a refusal, or asks "how much and when?".
- **Design handling:** promise_date.vague (ask once, then propose the deadline) exists. No rule covers an amount proposed with no date at all: the agent might default to today or to attempt 1, or class the turn as a non-answer.
- **Fix:** §7.9 / §5.3 `amount_without_date`: keep the amount as a pending proposal and ask once "On which day?" (an exact ask, not an amount ask). A vague answer gets r21 (propose the deadline). A today reading must say "today" in the read-back.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-31 Vague partial amount ("part of it", "something", "whatever I can")  `gap` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 4821, 420 / 126, early band. Customer: "I can pay part of it today."
- **Expected:** A vague amount is not a proposal, and it implies the full amount is too much. Make one floor offer on the customer's date (today): "the minimum payment of 126 dollars today; the rest stays overdue." Yes, read-back, yes. Ledger: [(p1, 126.0, 2026-10-14)], close_call(promise). Never ask how much.
- **Rule:** A r24, r26; unspecified: a vague partial amount counts as "full too much", and a date the customer named takes priority over the attempt-1 date
- **Failure mode:** The agent asks "how much can you pay today?" (rule 24), treats the reply as a refusal and proposes 420 on Friday, or records the full amount for today.
- **Design handling:** Not handled. Vague partial amounts ("part of it", "something", "whatever I can") have no lexicon. They are likely parsed as None, leading to an unclear re-ask or a refusal, and §5.3 floor_offer_date would also ignore the customer's "today".
- **Fix:** §7.10: a vague-partial lexicon counts as a too_much signal (keeping any date the customer named). The single floor offer goes on the customer's valid date (see AMT-32), never an amount question.
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-32 "Too much" together with the customer's own date  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Personal loan 780 / 260, late band. Customer: "The full amount is too much, but I could pay something on the 20th."
- **Expected:** One floor offer on the customer's valid date: "260 dollars on Tuesday 20 October; the rest stays overdue." Ledger: [(p1, 260.0, 2026-10-20)], close_call(promise).
- **Rule:** A r26, r29, r19; the floor_offer_date default applies only when no date was given
- **Failure mode:** The agent uses the attempt-1 date (Friday 16 October) and ignores the customer's 20th, so the ledger date mismatches. Or it asks how much "something" is.
- **Design handling:** §5.3 floor_offer_date says outright that the floor offer uses the attempt-1 date, with no exception for a date the customer named, so the offer is made for 10-16 instead of 10-20.
- **Fix:** Change §5.3 floor_offer_date to: the customer's valid named date if any (after the r20/r23 corrections), else the attempt-1 date. Apply the same to below_floor.date.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-33 Floor refused, then attempt 2 (floor on the deadline) in the late band  `covered` · high likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 1903, 2125.10 / 637.50, days_late 12 (late, deadline 2026-10-23). "Too much." Agent: 637.50 on Friday 16 October, the rest stays overdue. Customer: "No, Friday doesn't work." Attempt 2 is accepted. Twin: the same with days_late 6 (early).
- **Expected:** Late band: attempt 2 is 637.50 on the deadline. Ledger: [(p1, 637.5, 2026-10-23)], close_call(promise). Early twin: no attempt 2, so promises [] and close_call(no_promise, refused).
- **Rule:** A r26 ("Attempt 2 may name the floor again, on the deadline"), r30, r31, r18
- **Failure mode:** Attempt 2 offers the full 2125.10 on the deadline. Or the agent repeats the floor on Friday, makes attempt 2 in the early band, or asks the customer for a date and amount.
- **Design handling:** Ladder rung 2 (floor on deadline, late band only) per §4.3 negotiation.ladders. A date refusal with no new date is a flat refusal, no_repeat_refused_offer applies, and band.attempts stops the early twin.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-34 "Too much" said only after attempt 1 proposed the full amount  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 4821, 420 / 126, early band. Today-ask: "No." This is a flat refusal, so attempt 1 proposes 420 on Friday 16 October. Customer: "420 by Friday is too much." Then accepts the minimum.
- **Expected:** The too-much statement triggers rule 26: one floor offer, 126 on Friday 16 October, with the rest stays overdue. Ledger: [(p1, 126.0, 2026-10-16)], close_call(promise). If that is refused, the early band is spent: close no_promise/refused.
- **Rule:** A r26, r30; unspecified (U-1): the floor offer goes on the same attempt-1 date
- **Failure mode:** The agent treats "too much" as a refusal of attempt 1 and closes refused without offering the floor, or offers the floor on the deadline (attempt-2 behaviour in the early band).
- **Design handling:** With attempt_definition "an attempt = one proposal", attempt 1 (420 on Friday) is spent. A later too-much would make the floor offer a second proposal, which the early band does not allow, so the agent may close refused with no floor offer. Whether amounts.too_much.times is independent of the attempts left is not stated.
- **Fix:** §7.9: a too-much reply to a full-amount rung is not a refusal. It triggers the single floor offer on that rung's date, which re-does that attempt without consuming a new one, whatever the attempts left. Add a §5.3 row and a twin scenario (early band: full, too much, floor, accept).
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-35 Customer names "the minimum" or "the instalment" instead of a number  `gap` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief B, now 2026-10-14. p1 card 220 / min 66, p2 personal loan 640 / instalment 213, p3 car loan 75 / instalment 25. Customer: "I'll pay just the minimum on each of them on Friday." Brief A variant on a loan: "just the monthly instalment".
- **Expected:** Map each product to its own floor. These are customer proposals inside the range, so there is no floor-offer script and no "cannot be recorded". One combined read-back. Ledger: [(p1, 66.0, 2026-10-16), (p2, 213.0, 2026-10-16), (p3, 25.0, 2026-10-16)], close_call(promise).
- **Rule:** A r25, r27, r29; B r7
- **Failure mode:** The agent asks "what is your minimum?" (rule 24), uses minimum_payment on the loans, or ignores the proposal and pushes the full amounts as attempt 1.
- **Design handling:** No resolver for named references ("the minimum", "the instalment", "the monthly payment", "in full") or for "on each of them". u_scope is undefined, and the agent could ask "what is your minimum?" or ignore the proposal.
- **Fix:** §7.3/§7.9: named-amount lexicon -> NAMED(floor|full), resolved per product from types[type].floor / past_due. u_scope=each/all applies it to every remaining product. These are customer proposals (r27 in range), so no floor-offer script runs, and one combined read-back follows.
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-36 Counter-proposal after a floor offer is a proposal, not a refusal  `covered` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 1903, 2125.10 / 637.50, late band. After the floor offer (637.50 on Friday): "No, but I can do seven hundred on Friday." Variant: "No, but I can do five hundred."
- **Expected:** 700 is in range, so it is accepted and no attempt is used. Ledger: [(p1, 700.0, 2026-10-16)]. Variant: 500 cannot be recorded, and the floor has already been offered, so do not offer it again on Friday. Treat this as a flat refusal, so attempt 2 is 637.50 on 2026-10-23.
- **Rule:** A r29, r27, r26, r31
- **Failure mode:** "No, but 700" is counted as a refusal of the floor, so attempt 2 offers 637.50 on 10-23; the customer accepts and the ledger is wrong. In the variant the floor is offered twice on the same date.
- **Design handling:** negotiation.proposal_is_never_refusal (r29) makes "No, but 700" a proposal, and it is accepted. In the variant, below_floor.times=1 is spent, so `then: flat_refusal` leads to the next rung (attempt 2, floor on the deadline).
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-37 Customer's amount kept when the date is corrected  `partial` · high likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Personal loan 780 / 260, late band (deadline 2026-10-23). Customer: "I can pay four hundred on the 6th of November." Variant: "four hundred on Saturday."
- **Expected:** The amount 400 is in range, and the date is past the deadline, so rule 23 applies: say the latest date that can be recorded is Friday 23 October and offer 400 then. Ledger: [(p1, 400.0, 2026-10-23)]. Saturday variant: next business day, giving [(p1, 400.0, 2026-10-19)].
- **Rule:** A r23, r20, r27
- **Failure mode:** The deadline offer reverts to the full 780 (a template that uses past_due), or to the floor 260 (confused with attempt 2), so the amount in the ledger is wrong.
- **Design handling:** promise_date.after_deadline=offer_deadline and non_business_within_deadline=offer_next_business_day exist, but the design does not say the corrective offer keeps the customer's proposed amount. A template could re-derive the amount from the rung (full or floor).
- **Fix:** §7.9: corrective date offers carry the pending proposal's validated amount unchanged, and only the date is replaced. They consume no attempt (see AMT-06). Add a twin scenario.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-38 Hardship with an amount the customer offers unprompted  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Personal loan 780 / 260, late band. Customer: "I lost my job last month, but I can still pay three hundred on Friday." Variant: "...but I can pay fifty."
- **Expected:** One short sentence of sympathy and no persuasion. The volunteered 300 is in range: read back, confirm, record. Make the support offer once. If declined, close promise; if accepted, transfer to support and close transferred/support. Ledger: [(p1, 300.0, 2026-10-16)], close_call(promise). Variant: say 50 cannot be recorded and do not push the floor (default). Support declined: promises [], close no_promise/hardship.
- **Rule:** A r32 tail ("record the promise under sections 7 and 8"), r27; unspecified for below the floor during hardship (U-17)
- **Failure mode:** The agent ignores the amount and goes straight to the support offer and a hardship close, or pushes the full amount or floor during hardship. Or it closes hardship although a promise was recorded.
- **Design handling:** The intent action sympathy_offer_transfer with suspend_persuasion and keep_recorded exists, and outcomes precedence decides promise vs hardship. Not specified: how a proposal volunteered during hardship goes through r27 without persuasion, and the below-floor case during hardship (the I-22 default is not in §5.3).
- **Fix:** §5.3 `hardship_proposal`: in hardship mode a customer's proposal is validated under r27/r20-23. In range: read back and record. Below the floor: say it cannot be recorded, with no floor offer (below_floor.offer suppressed when suspend_persuasion). The support offer is made once. Outcome: promise if one was recorded, else hardship or transfer.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-39 Recurring or split amounts count as a plan request  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 4821, 420 / 126. Customer: "I could do fifty a month until it's paid off." Or: "Half now and half at the end of the month."
- **Expected:** This is a request for a payment plan or lower instalments. Describe no plan; call transfer_to_agent(queue=restructuring), then close. Ledger: promises [], transfers [restructuring], close_call(transferred, restructuring). If job loss, illness or a death is also mentioned, rule 32 comes first and the support team is offered.
- **Rule:** A r41, r33, r36
- **Failure mode:** The agent parses "fifty" as a one-off amount below the floor, says it cannot be recorded and offers the floor. Or it records half (210) as a single promise, or describes a split.
- **Design handling:** A restructure intent (Spec examples) and §5.3 intent_tie (hardship > restructure > too_much) exist. No rule says a recurring or split amount ("fifty a month", "half now and half later") is a restructure request rather than a one-off amount proposal.
- **Fix:** §7.10: a recurrence/split lexicon (a/per month, each week, until paid off, X now and X later, in N payments) maps to the restructure intent and overrides any amount proposal in that turn. Add it to the generic u_topic examples.
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-40 Amount units or fields changed in the hidden tool file  `covered` · low likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Hidden brief: get_account returns past_due_cents 42000 and min_due_cents 12600, plus a separate balance 3900, and create_promise takes amount_cents (integer). The customer agrees to the full amount on Friday.
- **Expected:** Speak "420 dollars". Send amount_cents=42000. The "full amount" is the field the brief names (past due), not balance. The ledger stores the promise in the tool's unit, matching the expected 42000.
- **Rule:** Hackathon: "fields and allowed values can change"; A r17/r24 analogues
- **Failure mode:** Field names hard-coded as minimum_payment, instalment_amount or past_due resolve to None. Or the agent speaks "42,000 dollars", sends 420 to a cents field, or offers the full balance.
- **Design handling:** §4.3 ApiRef `scale` 1|100 ("divided for speech and multiplied for the wire"), openapi_model detects cents by name/description, products.fields maps past_due separately from balance, amounts.first is an AmountRule, and the T4 mutant includes "amount in cents".
- **Test:** builder

#### AMT-41 Floor set by an amending memo (formula, rounding, effective date)  `covered` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Raw-material brief: a memo says "From 2026-11-01 the minimum we accept on car loans is 50% of the past-due amount, rounded up to the whole dollar." now 2026-11-03 (Tue), car loan past_due 1250.50, days_late 10, instalment_amount 400. "Too much." Twin: now 2026-10-28.
- **Expected:** On 11-03 the floor is ceil(625.25) = 626. Offer it once on attempt-1 date Friday 2026-11-06. Ledger: [(p1, 626.0, 2026-11-06)]. On the 10-28 twin the memo is not yet in force, so the floor is 400 on Friday 2026-10-30, giving [(p1, 400.0, 2026-10-30)].
- **Rule:** Hidden brief memo, which replaces A r25; the effective date is resolved against now
- **Failure mode:** The agent keeps the old instalment floor, ignores the effective date, rounds half up to 625.25 or 625, or applies the memo to every product type.
- **Design handling:** Dated<T> on every leaf with resolve_at=now for policy leaves (floors), AmountRule percent_of_full with rounding: ceil, a memo scoped to one product type splits the element (§5.2 step 6), oracle items for dated rules, and T4 "memo scoped to one product type".
- **Test:** builder

#### AMT-42 Floor mentioned before the full amount was asked  `covered` · medium likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 4821, 420 / 126. A debt statement drafted by an LLM: "...420 dollars past due, 6 days late; your minimum payment is 126. Can you make this payment today?"
- **Expected:** The debt statement gives the product, the past-due amount and the days late only. The today-ask is about the full amount. The floor appears only after "too much", a vague partial amount, or a proposal below the floor. Ledger as for the full-amount path, for example a customer who pays in full today: [(p1, 420.0, 2026-10-14)].
- **Rule:** A r17, r24 ("Ask for the full past-due amount first"), r26
- **Failure mode:** The customer anchors on 126 ("I'll pay the minimum"), so the ledger shows 126 where the expected full amount was. The judge flags that the full amount was not asked first, and the floor is then named twice.
- **Design handling:** The statement is a code-rendered LineRef from the Spec (products.statement_item, from r17). Floor facts are staged after too_much (§4.3 qa_facts_policy.staging), rung0 is the first ask, and there is no LLM-drafted statement (P3).
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-43 Customer asks how much would stay overdue  `partial` · medium likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 1903, 2125.10 / 637.50, late band, asks_back style. After the floor offer: "Wait, how much would still be overdue then?"
- **Expected:** Answer from the tool data only: 2,125.10 minus 637.50 = 1,487.60, or simply "the remaining past-due amount". Invent no interest, fees or credit-score consequences, and do not repeat the floor as a new offer. Re-ask neutrally ("Would that work for you?"). Ledger if accepted: [(p1, 637.5, 2026-10-16)].
- **Rule:** A r26, r44, r33
- **Failure mode:** Wrong arithmetic or float noise ("1487.6000000000001"). Or the agent invents "plus late fees", or re-offers the floor in full, which the check counts as a second offer.
- **Design handling:** The q_neg fence allows only the facts. The facts list (product, past_due, days_late, deadline, floor, agreed) has no remainder, so the answer is no_info, or the LLM does the arithmetic and may produce float noise. The <rest> placeholder exists but is not a fact.
- **Fix:** §4.3 qa_facts_policy: add a `rest` fact, computed in cents by code (past_due - pending offer), staged while an offer below full is pending. Keep the neutral re-ask after the answer. Interest and fees stay no_info.
- **Test:** chat

#### AMT-44 Digits with thousands separators  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14 (Wed). Car loan, past_due 1250.00, days_late 14 (late band, deadline 2026-10-23), instalment_amount 400. The customer types digits (not in_words style): "I can pay $1,250 on Friday." Variant on card 1903 (2125.10 / 637.50): "I can do 1,000 on Friday" and "2,125.10 Friday".
- **Expected:** Parse 1,250 as 1250.0, which equals the full amount, and accept it. Read back "car loan, 1,250 dollars, Friday 16 October. Do you confirm?", then create_promise(p1, 1250.0, 2026-10-16) and close as promise. In the variant, 1,000 is between the floor and the full amount: (p1, 1000.0, 2026-10-16).
- **Rule:** A r27, r34
- **Failure mode:** The parser splits on the comma and reads 1 or 250, or reads European style as 1.25. The amount then counts as below the floor, so the agent makes a floor offer and records the floor, or records 1.25. An LLM-written body may also send "1,250", which float() cannot parse.
- **Design handling:** parse_num handles digits, but thousands separators and decimal commas are not specified.
- **Fix:** §7.3: a comma followed by exactly 3 digits is a thousands separator, while a comma plus 2 digits at the end is a decimal only when there are no other separators (see AMT-77). Strip $ and currency first. Add "$1,250", "1,000" and "2,125.10" to §8.1.
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-45 "Yes" to the today-ask with a partial amount  `partial` · high likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 4821, 420 / 126, days_late 6 (early band). Agent: "Can you make this payment today?" Customer: "Yes, I can pay two hundred today." Variant: "Yes, I'll pay the minimum today."
- **Expected:** The "yes" covers today, not the full amount. 200 is between the floor and the full amount, so accept it with today's date. Read back 200 dollars, 14 October, and on a clear yes call create_promise(p1, 200.0, 2026-10-14). Close as promise. In the variant the amount is the floor: (p1, 126.0, 2026-10-14). No attempt is used.
- **Rule:** A r28, r29, r27
- **Failure mode:** An intent classifier sees "yes" and fills in the full amount, so the read-back says 420. The persona may confirm a read-back that sounds close enough, which records (420, 10-14). The agent may also go on to persuade for the remaining 220.
- **Design handling:** §6.5: a grounded amount in a future pay clause is a proposal, but there is no precedence rule when u_act=yes to the rung-0 ask comes with a different amount. A yes could fill in the full amount.
- **Fix:** §7.9: on any pending offer, a yes that carries a grounded amount or date different from the offer is a proposal of those values (r27/r28/r29), not acceptance of the offer. No attempt is used. The read-back uses the customer's values.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-46 "Yes" at the read-back, but with a different figure  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Personal loan, 780 / 260, late band. Agent: "personal loan, 300 dollars, Friday 16 October. Do you confirm?" Customer: "Yes, three hundred and fifty on Friday, that's right." Or: "Yeah, wait, three fifty, I said three fifty."
- **Expected:** This is not a clear yes. Treat it as a change at the read-back: check 350 against sections 7 and 8 (it is in range) and read it back again. Call create_promise only after a clean yes: (p1, 350.0, 2026-10-16). Close as promise.
- **Rule:** A r34, r35
- **Failure mode:** The yes or no detector fires on "yes" and records 300, so the ledger has the wrong amount. A second failure: the agent records 300 and then says it recorded 350, which fails the honesty check.
- **Design handling:** §4.3 require_clear_yes and on_change=revalidate_then_readback exist, but "clear yes" is not defined against a differing figure in the same message. A yes classifier could record 300.
- **Fix:** §7.11: a confirmation is a clear yes only if u_text contains no grounded amount, date or product that differs from the read-back. Otherwise it is a change: re-validate and read back again.
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-47 Amount change requested after the promise is recorded  `covered` · medium likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 4821, 420 / 126. create_promise(p1, 420, 2026-10-16) returned ok and the agent said the text-message sentence. Customer: "Actually, can we make that two hundred instead?" B variant: after all three create_promise calls, "lower the loan one to the instalment".
- **Expected:** Say the promise cannot be changed in this call and that the customer can change it in the mobile app. Make no second create_promise and do not reopen the negotiation. The ledger keeps the single (p1, 420.0, 2026-10-16). Thank the customer, then close as promise.
- **Rule:** A r36
- **Failure mode:** The agent calls create_promise again. The bank returns "this product already has a promise", and the agent then says the promise was updated (honesty failure). Or it re-runs the read-back and loops toward the turn limit.
- **Design handling:** recording.after_record_change LineRef (r36) is used. Unrolled write nodes with entry guards (§6.3) and ctl state forbid a second create for the product, and timeout_then_already_exists is handled.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-48 One amount for each product (Brief B)  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal

If the customer accepts both offers, make one combined read-back, then three creates: [(p1,100.0,2026-10-16),(p2,213.0,2026-10-16),(p3,75.0,2026-10-16)]. Close as promise.

- **Failure mode:** The agent reads "100 each" as a total of 100 to split, or records 100 on all three: one is above the full amount and one is below the floor. Or it applies only p1's validation to every product.
- **Design handling:** u_scope exists but is not defined. With a single u_amt, "a hundred on each" lands only on the current product, or is read as a total.
- **Fix:** §7.10: u_scope=each applies the amount to every remaining product and validates each separately (r27 in range / below floor with a single floor offer / above full gives an offer of full). The corrections go into one turn, then one combined read-back.

Go through them in order, and for each make its own single floor offer on Friday 2026-10-16 with "the rest stays overdue": 66, then 213, then 25. (a) Combined read-back, then [(p1,66.0,10-16),(p2,213.0,10-16),(p3,25.0,10-16)], close as promise. (b) p1 and p2 get attempt 2 (the floor on 2026-10-23). p3 is early band, so the call stops after one offer. Notes refused for p1, p2 and p3; close as no_promise / refused.
- **Rule:** B r4, r5; A r26, r30
- **Failure mode:** The blanket "too much" is treated as a flat refusal, so the agent proposes the full amounts first. Or the floor is offered only for p1. Or all three floors are offered in one breath and counted as one offer, which leaves the attempt counts wrong. Or the agent believes the floor may be offered only once per call.
- **Design handling:** §7.9 has a per-product too-much flag, but nothing applies a blanket "it's all too much" to every product. §5.3 attempt_definition only says a blanket refusal moves to the next product's attempt 1.
- **Fix:** §7.10: too_much with scope all ("all/everything/it's all") sets the flag on every unresolved product. Each then gets its own single floor offer as attempt 1, in get_account order, one product per turn. A refusal leads to the per-product rung 2 per band.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-50 "The loan" when two loans exist, or "the card" when two cards exist  `gap` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief B, now 2026-10-14. p1 card 220 / 66, p2 personal loan 640 / 213, p3 car loan 75 / 25. Customer: "I'll pay two hundred on the loan on Friday." 200 is below p2's floor and above p3's full amount. Variant: two credit cards (ending 2288 and 5512) and "the minimum on the card".
- **Expected:** Ask which product the customer means ("the personal loan or the car loan?"). This asks for a product, not an amount. Then check 200 against that product. Personal loan: below the floor, so it cannot be recorded and 213 is offered once. Car loan: above the full amount, so offer 75. Never attach an amount to a guessed product_id.
- **Rule:** B r1, r4; A r27; unspecified: clarify product references
- **Failure mode:** The agent attaches the amount to the product it is currently on, or to the first loan, so the ledger gets the wrong product_id or the wrong amount. A spurious floor offer may also be made.
- **Design handling:** There is a u_prod slot, but no rule for an ambiguous product reference. An amount may be attached to the current product or the first match.
- **Fix:** §7.10: resolve u_prod against the products' spoken forms, type words and display digits. More than one match: ask a product clarification question (exact repeat; not an amount ask) and hold the amount. One match: validate against that product.
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-51 Amount for a later product volunteered early (Brief B)  `partial` · low likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief B, now 2026-10-14. Same three products. The agent is on p1 (the card) at attempt 1 (220 on Friday). Customer: "Let's do the car loan first, I'll pay that one in full today." Then the customer accepts the card at 220 on Friday and the loan at 640 on Friday.
- **Expected:** Keep p3 (75, 2026-10-14) as agreed. Do not ask about today again and do not use any attempt on p3. Finish p1, then p2. The combined read-back lists all three, then [(p1,220.0,10-16),(p2,640.0,10-16),(p3,75.0,10-14)]. Close as promise.
- **Rule:** B r4, r7
- **Failure mode:** The current-product pointer applies "in full today" to p1, giving (p1, 220, today). Or the agent drops the p3 statement and later proposes p3 at attempt 1 on Friday, which records the wrong date.
- **Design handling:** Product-scoped intents act on the current product. A proposal naming a later product is not specified, so it can be attached to the current product or dropped.
- **Fix:** §7.9: a proposal with a resolved u_prod other than the current product is validated and stored as agreed for that product, and the loop later skips it (no attempts, no today re-ask). It is included in the combined read-back.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-52 Combined read-back: one product changed to below its floor (Brief B)  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief B, now 2026-10-14. p1 card 220 / 66 (late), p2 personal loan 640 / 213 (late), p3 car loan 75 / 25 (early). Everything is agreed in full for Friday. At the combined read-back: "The card and the car loan are fine, but on the personal loan I can only do a hundred." The customer then refuses 213 on Friday and 213 on the 23rd.
- **Expected:** 100 is below 213, so it cannot be recorded. Offer 213 on Friday once, with "the rest stays overdue". On a refusal, attempt 2 (late band) proposes 213 on 2026-10-23. When that is also refused, p2 is refused. Read p1 and p3 back again, then promises [(p1,220.0,10-16),(p3,75.0,10-16)], add_note(p2, refused), close as promise.
- **Rule:** B r7, r8; A r35, r27, r30
- **Failure mode:** The agent records p2 at 100 (below the floor). Or it records nothing because the single confirmation was broken. Or it forgets the p2 note, or writes the note before the creates.
- **Design handling:** on_change re-validates (§7.11), and below_floor, ladder and notes rules exist. Not specified: a change at the combined read-back that makes one product invalid sends only that product back to NEG while the others stay agreed, then the remaining items are read back again.
- **Fix:** §7.11: when a change is invalid for product k, set phase NEG(k) with the others kept as agreed. After k resolves (agreed or refused), return to CONF with all agreed items, then create the promises, then add the note for k before close.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-53 An earlier product's amount changed mid-loop (Brief B)  `partial` · low likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief B, now 2026-10-14. p1 card 220 / 66 is agreed in full for Friday. While the agent negotiates p2 (personal loan 640 / 213), the customer says: "Actually, for the card make it just the minimum." The customer then agrees to p2 in full on Friday.
- **Expected:** Change p1 to 66 (in range, same date). Keep p2's state and continue with p2, then p3. The combined read-back has the card at 66. Ledger: (p1, 66.0, 2026-10-16) plus the other agreed promises.
- **Rule:** B r4, r7; A r35, r27
- **Failure mode:** "The minimum" is attached to the current product, so p2 gets 213 and p1 stays at 220. Or the agent ignores the change because p1 is already "done".
- **Design handling:** No rule covers a change to an earlier, already agreed product while another product is being negotiated. "The minimum" lands on the current product.
- **Fix:** Use the AMT-51/AMT-35 resolvers: a u_prod reference to an agreed product updates that product's agreed amount after r27 validation and keeps the current product's state.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-54 Below the floor and after the deadline in one proposal  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Personal loan, 780 / 260, late band (deadline 2026-10-23). Customer: "I can pay fifty on the sixth of November." Variant: card 4821 (420 / 126, early): "five hundred on Saturday".
- **Expected:** Fix both problems in one counter-offer. 50 cannot be recorded, and the latest date that can be recorded is 23 October, so offer the floor 260 on 23 October, once, with "the rest stays overdue". If accepted: (p1, 260.0, 2026-10-23). Variant: above the full amount and a weekend day, so offer 420 on Monday 19 October and record (p1, 420.0, 2026-10-19) if accepted.
- **Rule:** A r20, r23, r27; unspecified: apply both corrections in one offer
- **Failure mode:** The agent fixes only one problem: it records 50 on 23 October, or 260 on 6 November. Or it offers the floor on Friday and then again on the deadline, naming the floor twice. Or it treats the combination as a refusal.
- **Design handling:** The amount corrections (below_floor, above_full) and date corrections (after_deadline, non-business day) exist separately. Applying both in one counter-offer is not specified, so the agent may fix only one problem or name the floor twice.
- **Fix:** §7.9 neg.correct(proposal): apply every amount correction and every date correction at once and produce one counter-offer. A below-floor correction counts as the single floor offer.
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-55 Customer's own partial amount, then the date is refused: which amount the attempts use  `partial` · medium likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Personal loan, 780 / 260, late band. Customer: "I can pay four hundred on the sixth of November." Agent: the latest date is 23 October, offers 400 on the 23rd. Customer: "No, I can't do it before the sixth." The customer then refuses everything (twin script: accepts the instalment on the 23rd).
- **Expected:** Refusing the deadline counts as a flat refusal (r23). Attempt 1 is the full 780 on Friday 16 October: the customer never said "too much", so the literal rule 30 applies. Attempt 2 is 260 on 23 October. Never repeat "400 on the 23rd". Main script: no promise, close as no_promise / refused. Twin script: (p1, 260.0, 2026-10-23), close as promise.
- **Rule:** A r23, r30, r31 (amount for attempt 1 after a customer's partial amount is unspecified; literal reading: the full amount)
- **Failure mode:** The agent repeats the refused 400-on-the-23rd offer (breaks r31). Or it counts the deadline offer as an attempt and stops after one more. Or it closes at once, leaving out attempt 2, which the judge checks in the late band.
- **Design handling:** offered_date_refused=flat_refusal (U-14) applies. But attempt_definition ("an attempt = one proposal") counts the 400-on-the-23rd correction as attempt 1, so the full-on-Friday attempt 1 would be skipped. Which amount attempt 1 uses after a customer's partial amount is not stated.
- **Fix:** Same attempt_definition fix as AMT-06 (corrective offers consume no attempt). §5.3: after a refused corrective offer, attempt 1 uses the full amount unless the too-much flag is set. no_repeat_refused_offer is keyed on the (amount, date) pair.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-56 Repeated haggling below the floor after the single floor offer  `covered` · medium likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 4821, 420 / 126, early band. "I can do fifty." Agent: 50 cannot be recorded; offers 126 by Friday 16 October; the rest stays overdue. Customer: "How about a hundred?" Late-band variant: personal loan 780 / 260. Creeping variant: "Fine, a hundred and fifty then."
- **Expected:** Say 100 cannot be recorded either. Do not make a second floor pitch. Not accepting the floor is a flat refusal (r27). Early band: attempts are used up, so close as no_promise / refused with no promises. Late band: attempt 2 offers 260 on 2026-10-23; if accepted, (p1, 260.0, 2026-10-23). Creeping variant: 150 is valid, so accept it with the pending date, (p1, 150.0, 2026-10-16).
- **Rule:** A r27 vs r29 (unspecified tie: below-floor counters after the floor offer count as not accepting the floor)
- **Failure mode:** The agent loops, saying "cannot be recorded" and the floor again and again, until the turn limit. Or it accepts 100, or asks "what can you manage?". Or it treats 150 as a refusal.
- **Design handling:** below_floor.times=1 and then: flat_refusal: a second below-floor counter gets the cannot-be-recorded line with no offer, then the next rung (early band: stop; late band: attempt 2). A valid creep (150) is an in-range proposal and is accepted (r29).
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-57 "Too much" and a below-floor amount in the same turn  `partial` · medium likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 1903, 2125.10 / 637.50, late band. Customer: "That's way too much. I could maybe do a hundred on Friday." The customer then accepts the minimum.
- **Expected:** Make exactly one floor offer, covering both rule 26 and rule 27: "100 dollars cannot be recorded; the minimum payment is 637.50 dollars by Friday 16 October; the rest stays overdue." If accepted: (p1, 637.5, 2026-10-16), close as promise.
- **Rule:** A r26, r27
- **Failure mode:** Two handlers fire, one for "too much" and one for below the floor, so the floor is named twice and the judge check "minimum offered once" fails. Or the agent accepts 100.
- **Design handling:** §4.3 has two separate counters (too_much.times, below_floor.times). When both fire in one turn, the floor could be named twice, and no shared counter is specified.
- **Fix:** §7.9: one floor_offered flag per product shared by r26 and r27. A turn with both signals composes one line: below_floor.say + floor offer + say_rest.
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-58 "Too much" said in other words  `partial` · high likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 4821, 420 / 126, early band. Today-ask. Customer: "I can't pay all of that.", "I can't afford that much." or "Not the whole thing, no." There is no date and no amount. The customer then accepts the minimum on Friday.
- **Expected:** Treat it as rule 26 "too much", not a flat refusal and not hardship. Offer 126 by Friday 16 October once, with "the rest stays overdue". Then (p1, 126.0, 2026-10-16), close as promise.
- **Rule:** A r26 vs r30 vs r32
- **Failure mode:** Classed as a flat refusal: attempt 1 proposes 420 on Friday, the early band's single attempt is used up, and the call may close as refused. Or "can't afford" is classed as hardship, so the agent offers support and closes as no_promise / hardship.
- **Design handling:** too_much detection depends on Spec intent examples. §5.3 intent_tie puts hardship above too_much, but "can't afford that much" could be read as hardship, and paraphrases ("not the whole thing") may land on a flat refusal.
- **Fix:** §6.5: give the generic u_topic too_much template built-in paraphrases (can't pay all of that, can't afford that much, not the whole thing). Hardship needs the brief's named triggers (illness, death, job loss); "afford" alone is not hardship. Calibrate in E4.
- **Test:** chat

#### AMT-59 "Nothing until payday" is a vague date, not zero  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Personal loan, 780 / 260, late band. Customer: "I can't pay anything until my salary comes in." When asked for the exact day: "the twentieth". Twin: "I don't know."
- **Expected:** This is a vague period, not a refusal and not an amount. Ask once for the exact day and use no attempt. The 20th is a Tuesday within the deadline: (p1, 780.0, 2026-10-20). Twin: propose the deadline, (p1, 780.0, 2026-10-23).
- **Rule:** A r21, r29, r30
- **Failure mode:** "Can't pay anything" triggers a flat refusal (attempt 1 at 780 on Friday) or the zero or hardship path, and the salary date is lost.
- **Design handling:** promise_date.vague (ask once, then deadline) exists. "Can't pay anything until my salary comes in" could be classed as zero, a refusal or hardship. The "until <event>" construction is not mapped to VAGUE.
- **Fix:** §7.4/§7.10: "until/when/after <payday|salary|paycheck|next week>" gives date=VAGUE with intent to pay. This overrides the zero/refusal reading and uses no attempt. Ask once, then propose the deadline.
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-60 A correction or retraction makes the amount invalid  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Personal loan, 780 / 260, late band. (a) corrects style, in the opposite direction to the earlier case: "I can pay three hundred, sorry, I mean two hundred, on Friday." (b) "I could do three hundred Friday... actually no, forget it, I can't pay anything."
- **Expected:** (a) The corrected value, 200, is below the floor: it cannot be recorded, so offer 260 on Friday once. If accepted: (p1, 260.0, 2026-10-16). (b) The retraction leaves no date and no amount, so it is a flat refusal. Attempt 1 is 780 on Friday 16 October, attempt 2 is 260 on 2026-10-23. If everything is refused: no_promise / refused.
- **Rule:** A r27, r29, r30; corrects style
- **Failure mode:** The agent keeps the first, valid value (300) and records it. Or in (b) it still treats 300 as a live proposal, or reads the retraction as hardship.
- **Design handling:** (a) is covered by the correction markers (§6.5). (b) A marker followed by a retraction with no new value is unspecified: "value after the last marker" is empty, so the slot's 300 may survive.
- **Fix:** §7.10: a correction or retraction marker followed by no amount or date voids the earlier value. With negation ("forget it, can't pay") it is a flat refusal under r30.
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-61 Amount given as alternatives or a range  `gap` · low likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 4821, 420 / 126. Customer: "I could do two hundred, maybe two-fifty, on Friday." Other forms: "somewhere between two and three hundred", "at least two hundred", "a couple hundred".
- **Expected:** Do not pick a value silently and do not ask "how much can you pay". Ask which of the customer's own figures to record ("Shall I record 200 or 250?"); "at least 200" is 200. Accept the value the customer chooses: for example (p1, 200.0, 2026-10-16). Read it back before recording.
- **Rule:** A r24, r27, r34; unspecified: clarify the customer's own alternatives
- **Failure mode:** The agent records the higher value or an average such as 225. Or it says "what amount can you pay?", which breaches rule 24.
- **Design handling:** Not handled. Several amounts not separated by a correction marker, ranges and "at least" have no rule, so the agent may pick one silently.
- **Fix:** §7.10: more than one amount without a correction marker, or a range, leads to a choice question naming only the customer's own figures ("Shall I record 200 or 250?"). "at least N" = N. "a couple hundred" = 200, confirmed in the read-back.
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-62 Named reference with a wrong figure ("the minimum, the six hundred")  `gap` · low likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 1903, 2125.10 / 637.50, late band. Customer: "I'll just pay the minimum, the six hundred, on Friday." Loan variant: personal loan 780 / 260: "Can I just pay the minimum?" A loan has no minimum, only an instalment.
- **Expected:** State the real figure from the tools: "The minimum payment is 637.50 dollars; shall I record 637.50 on Friday 16 October?" Then (p1, 637.5, 2026-10-16). Loan variant: the loan's floor is the instalment, 260.
- **Rule:** A r25, r27, r44
- **Failure mode:** The agent records 600, which is below the floor. Or it says 600 cannot be recorded and treats the rest as a refusal. Or it says a loan has no minimum and stops, or invents a figure.
- **Design handling:** No named-reference resolver, and no rule for when a named reference and a spoken figure conflict.
- **Fix:** With the AMT-35 resolver: NAMED(floor) takes the product's real floor. If a spoken figure conflicts, the agent states the real figure ("The minimum payment is 637.50 dollars; shall I record that on Friday 16 October?"). On a loan, "minimum" maps to the instalment floor.
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-63 Relative amount tied to the agent's last figure ("half of that", "same for the loan")  `gap` · low likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 4821, 420 / 126. Attempt 1: 420 by Friday. Customer: "I can do half of that." Variants: "fifty less than that" (370); after the floor offer on card 1903, "half of that?" (318.75, below the floor). B: after the card's floor of 66 is accepted, "same for the loan".
- **Expected:** Tie the amount to the figure last named. Half of 420 is 210, which is valid: (p1, 210.0, 2026-10-16). Half of 637.50 is 318.75, below the floor, so it counts as not accepting the floor. B: "same" is ambiguous (66 is below the loan's floor; the loan's floor is 213), so ask, and record 213 only if the customer means the loan's minimum.
- **Rule:** A r27; B r4
- **Failure mode:** The agent bases the fraction on the debt when the customer meant the offer, or the other way round. LLM arithmetic errors. Or in B it records 66 on the loan.
- **Design handling:** No relative-amount resolution against the agent's last figure, and no handling of "same for the loan".
- **Fix:** In the RELATIVE resolver (AMT-13): 'that' = the last figure the agent named for the current product. "less/more than that" applies the difference. "same" across products is ambiguous, so ask whether the customer means the same figure or that product's minimum, and never copy the figure to another product silently.
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-64 Customer disputes the amount but proposes their own figure  `partial` · medium likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Personal loan, 780 / 260, late band. Customer: "That's wrong, I only owe three hundred. I'll pay the three hundred on Friday."
- **Expected:** This is not a dispute of the debt: rule 40 covers only "not mine" or "never had it". Do not argue, and say only that the account shows 780. 300 is a customer proposal in [260, 780], so accept it: (p1, 300.0, 2026-10-16), close as promise. Do not suggest the remaining 480 is wrong or cleared.
- **Rule:** A r29, r40, r44 (amount disputes are unspecified; default: a proposal)
- **Failure mode:** The agent closes as no_promise / dispute. Or it argues and insists on 780. Or it agrees the debt is 300 (an honesty failure).
- **Design handling:** A dispute intent comes from the Spec (r40 examples), but no precedence is given between a dispute-like remark ("that's wrong, I only owe 300") and a grounded proposal in the same turn.
- **Fix:** §5.3 `amount_dispute`: dispute only on denial of the product or debt (not mine / never had it). A disagreement about the amount with a proposal is a proposal (r29). Fixed line: "The account shows <past_due> past due", and never agree with the customer's figure.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-65 Partial-payment claim with no proposal is not `paid`  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 4821, 420 / 126, early band. Customer: "I already paid the minimum, the 126, this morning in the app." No date or amount follows, and the customer refuses further offers.
- **Expected:** Rule 39 covers only a payment of this past-due amount, so do not close as paid. Do not argue; say the account still shows 420 past due (the delay sentence is fine), then continue the negotiation on 420 with no invented remainder. With the refusal: attempt 1 is 420 on Friday, then close as no_promise / refused with no promises.
- **Rule:** A r39 last sentence, r44, r30
- **Failure mode:** The agent closes as paid (wrong outcome). Or it proposes an invented remainder of 294 that the customer never named.
- **Design handling:** A paid intent comes from Spec examples. The r39 last sentence (only this past-due amount) may be captured in the Spec, but no generic code checks a past-tense partial amount against past_due.
- **Fix:** §7.10: the paid intent fires only when no past-tense amount below past_due is grounded. Otherwise use a fixed line (the account shows <past_due>; payments can take one business day to appear), continue negotiating on the full past_due, and never invent a remainder.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-66 Amount volunteered before verification  `partial` · low likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 4821, 420 / 126. While being asked for the date of birth, the customer says: "Look, I know what this is, I'll pay two hundred on Friday. Do you need my birthday?" The customer then answers both questions.
- **Expected:** Before verification, say nothing about the amount, the product or the debt. Finish both questions, call get_account, state the debt, make the today-ask, and keep or re-elicit the customer's 200 on Friday. Then (p1, 200.0, 2026-10-16), close as promise. This is not a refusal to verify.
- **Rule:** A r1, r11, r16, r17, r29
- **Failure mode:** The agent says "200 on your credit card" before verification (disclosure). Or it treats the reply as the "what is this about" decline. Or it later ignores the proposal and pushes the full 420.
- **Design handling:** Before verification only fixed tts and canned question answers are used, so there is no disclosure (§6.4, I10), and identity normalise reads only u_ans. decline_counting treats a question as a question. The volunteered proposal is not stashed, so it relies on the customer repeating it after ASK_FIRST.
- **Fix:** §7.16: stash a grounded pre-verification proposal in st, without speaking it. After the statement and the ask, the stashed proposal is applied as the customer's proposal (r29) once the customer answers.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-67 Floor refused before it is offered ("I can't even pay the minimum")  `gap` · medium likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 1903, 2125.10 / 637.50, late band. After the debt statement: "No way, I can't even pay the minimum." The customer refuses everything. Early twin: card 4821, 420 / 126.
- **Expected:** Treat it as "too much" plus a flat refusal. Attempt 1 is the floor 637.50 on Friday 16 October, once, with "the rest stays overdue". Attempt 2 is 637.50 on 23 October. Then close as no_promise / refused with no promises. Early twin: one floor offer, then close as no_promise / refused. Not hardship, so no support offer.
- **Rule:** A r26, r30, r31 (pre-emptive floor refusal is unspecified)
- **Failure mode:** The agent closes at once with zero attempts (fails the two-attempts check in the late band). Or it proposes the full amount on Friday. Or it asks how much they can pay. Or it treats the reply as hardship.
- **Design handling:** Not handled. "I can't even pay the minimum" is neither too_much nor a refusal in the lexicon, so it may close with zero attempts or offer the full amount.
- **Fix:** §7.10: a pre-emptive floor refusal sets the too-much flag and counts as a flat refusal. Attempt 1 is the floor on the attempt-1 date (r30 "floor if already too much") with say_rest. The late band then gets attempt 2 (floor on the deadline). Not hardship.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-68 Floor accepted but for a date after the deadline  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 1903, 2125.10 / 637.50, late band (deadline 2026-10-23). Floor offered for Friday. Customer: "The minimum's OK, but only on the 30th." The customer accepts the 23rd.
- **Expected:** Keep the floor amount and move only the date: "The latest date I can record is 23 October", and offer 637.50 on 23 October. Then (p1, 637.5, 2026-10-23), close as promise. This is not attempt 2.
- **Rule:** A r23, r26, r29
- **Failure mode:** The agent copies PUB-04's pattern and goes back to the full 2125.10 on the deadline. Or it counts the move as attempt 2 and later repeats it. Or it records the 30th.
- **Design handling:** promise_date.after_deadline=offer_deadline exists, but it does not say the floor amount is kept, or that the correction is not attempt 2 (attempt_definition counts any proposal).
- **Fix:** Same as AMT-37 and AMT-06: a corrective deadline offer keeps the pending amount (here the floor) and consumes no attempt.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-69 Card digits or days-late echoed back, where the number falls in the valid range  `gap` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 1903, 2125.10 / 637.50, days_late 12, talkative style. Customer: "The one ending nineteen-oh-three? Twelve days, really? Fine, I'll pay it Friday after five."
- **Expected:** There is no amount, so it is the amount on the table: the full amount on Friday, (p1, 2125.1, 2026-10-16). 1903, 12 and 5 are not amounts.
- **Rule:** A r27, r29; parse grounding
- **Failure mode:** 1903 falls inside [637.50, 2125.10], so it is silently accepted and the ledger gets (p1, 1903.0, 10-16). Or 12 or 5 is read as a below-floor amount, which triggers a needless floor offer.
- **Design handling:** Grounding (§6.5) only checks that the tokens are in u_text. 1903 (display digits), 12 (days_late) and 5 ("after five") all pass grounding, and 1903 is inside [637.50, 2125.10], so it would be silently accepted.
- **Fix:** §7.10: drop amount candidates that equal display fields, days_late or the account number, that are part of a time phrase (after/before/at N, o'clock), or that are dates. An amount must sit in a pay clause with a pay verb. With no amount, the offered or full amount stands.
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-70 Below-floor amount on a day other than Friday: date of the floor offer  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 4821, 420 / 126, early band. Customer: "I can only do fifty on Tuesday the twentieth." The customer accepts the minimum when it is offered.
- **Expected:** The customer's date is valid and is a proposal, so keep it. "50 cannot be recorded; the minimum is 126 by Tuesday 20 October; the rest stays overdue." Then (p1, 126.0, 2026-10-20), close as promise.
- **Rule:** A r27, r29; unspecified: U-1 puts the attempt-1 date only on a dateless offer
- **Failure mode:** The policy that puts the floor offer on the attempt-1 date fires mechanically and offers 126 on Friday 16 October. The persona accepts, and the ledger date differs from the expected 10-20.
- **Design handling:** below_floor has no date field, and §5.3 floor_offer_date sends floor offers to the attempt-1 date, so the customer's valid Tuesday the 20th would be replaced by Friday.
- **Fix:** Same as AMT-32 / AMT-11: below_floor.date and too_much.date default to the customer's valid named date, else the attempt-1 date.
- **Test:** twin

#### AMT-71 Cents in words that can be read two ways  `partial` · low likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 1903, 2125.10 / 637.50. Customer: "seven hundred and fifty dollars and five on Friday" (750.05), "six thirty-seven point five" (637.50), "seven fifty point oh five" (750.05), "seven hundred fifty and five" with no unit (755).
- **Expected:** "dollars and N" with no "cents" means N cents. "point five" is .50 and "point oh five" is .05. A bare "fifty and five" is ambiguous, so read back the parsed value (755) and accept a correction. Record exactly what the customer confirms, for example (p1, 750.05, 2026-10-16).
- **Rule:** A r27, r34
- **Failure mode:** "point five" is read as .05, so 637.05 falls below the floor and the agent makes a spurious floor offer. Or "dollars and five" is read as 755, or the cents are dropped.
- **Design handling:** Decimal and cents readings in words (point five vs point oh five, "dollars and five") are not specified in §7.3.
- **Fix:** §7.3 parse_num rules: 'point D' = D/10, 'point oh D' = D/100, 'point DD' = DD/100. '<N> dollars and <M>' with no unit = M cents when M < 100. A bare '<hundreds> and <M>' with no unit = N+M, which is always read back so the customer can correct it. Unit-test all four forms.
- **Test:** unit

#### AMT-72 Question about interest or fees on the rest  `covered` · medium likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief A, now 2026-10-14. Card 1903, 2125.10 / 637.50, late band. After the floor offer: "Will I get charged interest or a late fee on the rest if I only pay that?" The customer then accepts the minimum on Friday.
- **Expected:** Say you do not have that information. Invent no fee, no interest figure and no "no extra charges" assurance, and offer no waiver. Continue: (p1, 637.5, 2026-10-16), close as promise.
- **Rule:** A r44, r33
- **Failure mode:** The LLM reassures with made-up terms ("there's no extra charge", "a 25 dollar fee") or offers to waive fees, which fails the judge's honesty and policy checks.
- **Design handling:** The §6.4 q_* fence: "If the facts do not contain the answer, say exactly no_info... Do not mention any amount, date, plan, discount or term that is not in the facts", and never_offer covers waivers.
- **Test:** chat

#### AMT-73 "What's the total?" with several products (Brief B)  `partial` · low likelihood · minor
- **Scenario:** Brief B, now 2026-10-14. p1 card 220, p2 personal loan 640, p3 car loan 75. After the statements: "So how much is that altogether?"
- **Expected:** Either give the exact sum, 935 dollars, computed in code from get_account, or repeat each product's amount. Never give a wrong total. The question uses no attempt; then continue with the all-today ask.
- **Rule:** A r44 (no invented figures); B r2
- **Failure mode:** LLM arithmetic gives a wrong total (for example 925), or it adds the floors in. The judge flags dishonesty.
- **Design handling:** The facts list holds per-product past_due but no total, so the LLM in q_neg may add them up itself despite the fence.
- **Fix:** §4.3 qa_facts_policy: add a code-computed `total_past_due` fact (in cents) when there are 2 or more products.
- **Test:** chat

#### AMT-74 Hidden brief uses a currency other than dollars  `covered` · low likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Hidden raw-material brief: the mail and policy state amounts in EUR ("EUR 420.00"). get_account is unchanged (past_due 420, minimum_payment 126). The customer says "I'll pay a hundred and fifty dollars on Friday."
- **Expected:** The agent says amounts in the brief's currency ("euros") and never "dollars". The customer's word for the currency does not change the number: 150 is in range, so (p1, 150.0, 2026-10-16).
- **Rule:** unspecified: currency word comes from the brief (U-25)
- **Failure mode:** The builder hard-codes "dollars" from Brief A or PUB examples, so the judge flags an inaccurate statement of the debt. Or the agent questions or converts the customer's "dollars".
- **Design handling:** §4.3 bank.currency_word, §5.3 currency_word (the brief's word, else none) and D10. Speech never takes the customer's currency word, and parse_num strips currency words (§7.3).
- **Test:** builder

#### AMT-75 create_promise gains amount fields or an amount format  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Hidden tool file. create_promise.amount becomes {type: string, pattern: ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]{2}$}, plus a required currency enum [USD] and/or promise_type enum [full, minimum, partial]. The customer agrees to the minimum 637.50 on Friday.
- **Expected:** The body has amount "637.50" (two decimals as a string), currency "USD", and promise_type "minimum": the amount equals the floor, so it is minimum. An amount equal to past_due is full; anything else is partial. Ledger (p1, 637.5, 2026-10-16).
- **Rule:** OpenAPI binding (fields and enums may change)
- **Failure mode:** The builder still sends the number 637.5, or leaves out the new required fields, so the call returns ok:false. Two failures lead to no_promise / service_error. Or promise_type is chosen by an LLM rather than by a comparison.
- **Design handling:** ApiRef types (number/integer/string), extra_required with source/logged_default, and wire_format for dates exist. There is no amount string wire format from a pattern, and no runtime-derived enum source (promise_type from comparing the amount with full or floor). A required enum would be bound to a constant or guessed.
- **Fix:** §4.5: add an amount wire_format from type/pattern ('%.2f' string for the pattern ^\d+\.\d{2}$). A single-value enum (currency) gets a const source.
