- **Scenario:** Brief A, Mr Reyes. DOB '15 March 1988' (wrong), then '14 March 1988' (ok). Phone '4417' (wrong), then '4170' (wrong).
- **Expected:** The 3rd wrong answer in total ends the check: no 4th verify, no debt, the app/branch line, close not_verified/failed. After a phone miss, ask only for the phone again, never the DOB. Ledger: 4 verify calls, not_verified/failed, no get_account.
- **Rule:** A r12, r14; PUB-12 check 'phone asked again once, DOB not'
- **Failure mode:** A per-question counter allows a third phone try. Or the DOB is asked again after a phone miss. Or wrong_answers_left is ignored.
- **Design handling:** §4.3 identity.max_wrong_total, wrong_count_source api_remaining, per-question reask_wrong; one question at a time; on_failed after the total.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-59 Swapped day/month hint after two wrong answers  `covered` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, DOB 1979-11-02. The customer gives '3 November 1979' (wrong), '2 November 1978' (wrong), then 'eleven, two, seventy-nine' (month first). Read day first, that is 1979-02-11, and the result has hint 'day_month_swapped'.
- **Expected:** Send the day-first reading 1979-02-11, as r11 says. On the hint, ask for the month as a word. It does not count, so the check goes on. 'November' gives 1979-11-02, verified, then the phone question. Ledger: 2 wrong answers, check not ended, the case's normal outcome.
- **Rule:** A r11, r13, r12
- **Failure mode:** Counts the hint as the third wrong answer and closes not_verified/failed. Or silently swaps to month-first and skips the 'month as a word' step the judge may check. Or asks for the numbers again.
- **Design handling:** §4.3 identity.hints {counts_as_wrong false, say: ask for the month as a word}; numeric_order DMY default (§5.3).
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-60 Brief B: restructuring mid-loop drops agreed promises  `covered` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief B, now Wed 2026-10-14, PUB-11 products (card 2288 220/9 days, personal loan 640/9 days, car loan 75/3 days). All-today 'no'. p1: 'Friday is fine for the card.' p2: 'For the loan, can I get lower instalments?'
- **Expected:** Transfer at once with transfer_to_agent(restructuring). p1 was agreed but not recorded: no read-back, no create_promise, no text-message sentence, no notes. Goodbye, then close transferred/restructuring. Ledger: promises [], notes [], transfers [restructuring].
- **Rule:** B r10
- **Failure mode:** 'Record agreed items before closing' logic records p1 first. Or notes are written for p2/p3. Or the close is promise.
- **Design handling:** §4.3 action drop_unrecorded; §5.3 agreed_before_terminal skips drop_unrecorded intents (and transfers); notes none_if_transfer.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-61 Brief B: hardship across products  `covered` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** PUB-11 products. (a) At the all-today ask: 'My wife died last month, I can't deal with this.' Declines support. (b) p1 agreed for Fri 16 Oct, then the same hardship at p2; declines support. (c) As (b), but accepts support.
- **Expected:** One sympathy sentence, support offered once, no persuasion on any remaining product. (a) Notes (p1,hardship), (p2,hardship), (p3,hardship); close no_promise/hardship. (b) Read back p1 only, confirm, record p1 220.0 2026-10-16, say the text-message sentence, then notes (p2,hardship), (p3,hardship); close promise/null. (c) transfer support, no notes, p1 not recorded (default, by analogy with B r10); close transferred/support.
- **Rule:** A r32; B r8, r10, Closing; KB I-39
- **Failure mode:** No notes (Brief A habit), 'refused' notes, an attempt on p2/p3, or notes written around the support transfer.
- **Design handling:** §5.3 hardship_multi (no persuasion; a hardship note on each product without a promise); agreed_before_terminal reads back and records agreed items before a non-transfer close; transfer → no notes; precedence promise wins.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-62 Brief B: undiscussed products and reason precedence  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** PUB-11 products. (a) p1: 'That card was never mine.' Then at p2: 'I don't want to talk about this.' ... 'I said I don't want to talk.' (b) The customer says all three are already paid.
- **Expected:** (a) A note for EVERY product without a promise, including p3, which was never discussed: (p1,dispute), (p2,refused), (p3,refused). Close no_promise/dispute: B's closing rule (first non-paid note in get_account order) beats A r45's 'refused'. (b) Notes (p1,paid), (p2,paid), (p3,paid), the one-business-day sentence, then close paid with NO reason.
- **Rule:** B r8, r9, Closing; A r45, r39
- **Failure mode:** Notes only for products that were discussed. Or the r45 close no_promise/refused is used. Or the close sends reason 'paid' with outcome paid.
- **Design handling:** notes_scope covers products never discussed, and outcomes.precedence first_note_by api_order covers the closing reason. Not specified: the note reason for products never reached after a refuse-to-talk close, and whether B's first-note selector beats the r45 S_REFUSED_TO_TALK situation.
- **Fix:** §7.13: products never reached take the terminal situation's note_reason (refused). §7.8: when a notes rule is in force, the first_note_by selector takes precedence over from_terminal for no_promise closes. Add an oracle item.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-63 Brief B: correction during the joint read-back  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** PUB-11. Read-back: 'credit card ending 2288, 220; personal loan, 640; car loan, 75; all on Friday 16 October. Do you confirm?' Reply: 'The car loan on Thursday, sorry, the other two Friday.'
- **Expected:** Check 15 Oct for p3 (early band), read ALL three back again, ask one 'Do you confirm?', then make 3 create_promise calls. Ledger: p1 220.0 2026-10-16, p2 640.0 2026-10-16, p3 75.0 2026-10-15.
- **Rule:** B r7; A r35
- **Failure mode:** Creates p1/p2 before the new confirmation. Or applies Thursday to all three. Or asks for a confirmation per product (judge check: 'one confirmation').
- **Design handling:** confirmation.on_change revalidate_then_readback and readback_together exist. But §6.5 has a single u_date/u_prod slot, so 'the car loan on Thursday, the other two Friday' (two product-date pairs) cannot be represented.
- **Fix:** §7.4/§7.10: add a code clause splitter over u_text using product spoken forms and 'the other(s)/rest' as anchors, giving per-product date and amount pairs. Then revalidate each and read all back again with one confirm.
- **Test:** unit

#### JDG-64 Explicit repeat request vs neutral re-ask  `partial` · medium likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Attempt 1 pending: 'Could you pay 420 by Friday 16 October?' Customer: 'Sorry, which day was that?' Or, after the debt statement: 'How much did you say?'
- **Expected:** Say the fact again (same offer, same date or amount) and the same question. It is not a new attempt. A neutral 'Would that work for you?' is wrong here because it leaves the question unanswered.
- **Rule:** A r44 (answer questions), r31 (attempt counting)
- **Failure mode:** The design's neutral re-ask (RL2) ignores the question and the judge fails it for not answering. Or the repeat is counted as attempt 2 and the agent jumps to the floor.
- **Design handling:** A repeat request ('which day was that?') is u_act=question → q_*. The facts list (product, past_due, days_late, deadline, floor, agreed) does not include the pending offer's date or amount, and {{ask}} is the neutral form, so the question may go unanswered.
- **Fix:** Add a `repeat_request` act in §6.5/§7.10: re-say the pending ask exactly (exact repeat_mode), not counted as a new attempt. Add the pending offer to q_* facts.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-65 Hedged answers: 'I'll try', 'maybe', 'I suppose'  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** (a) Today-ask: 'I'll try.' / 'Maybe.' (b) Read-back 'Do you confirm?': 'I suppose... I'll do my best.'
- **Expected:** (a) A non-answer counts as a flat refusal, so make attempt 1 (Friday). Record nothing on 'I'll try'. (b) This is not a clear yes: ask 'Do you confirm?' once more and call create_promise only on a clear yes. If the answer is still hedged, record nothing (default: treat it as refusing that offer).
- **Rule:** A r30 ('a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt'), r34
- **Failure mode:** The yes/no classifier maps 'I'll try' to yes. A promise is recorded without a clear yes: the ledger has an unexpected promise and the judge fails it.
- **Design handling:** §6.5: unknown → unclear → one clarification re-ask, never a refusal; negotiation.non_answer_counts_as_refusal with clarify_unclear_first; confirmation.require_clear_yes. Hedges are not defined, and there is no rule for a second hedged reply at CONF.
- **Fix:** §7.10: a hedge lexicon (try, maybe, I suppose, do my best) = non-answer, never yes. At CONF: one 'Do you confirm?' re-ask, then treat it as refusing that offer (§7.11).
- **Test:** unit

#### JDG-66 Customer asks for the minimum or the latest date  `partial` · medium likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Brief A, car loan 1250, instalment 400, 14 days late (deadline 23 Oct). After the today-ask: 'What's the least I can pay?' or 'What's the latest I can pay?'
- **Expected:** Answer from the data. Minimum: offer the floor 400 once, saying the rest stays overdue; this is the single r26 floor offer. Latest date: 'The latest date I can record is Friday 23 October.' Neither question counts as a refusal. Never say 'I don't have that information' about data the tools returned.
- **Rule:** A r26, r23, r44 (only for what the tools cannot answer)
- **Failure mode:** Staged facts hide the floor or deadline, so the agent falsely says 'I don't have that information' (honesty), or makes up a figure.
- **Design handling:** The deadline is an allowed q_* fact, so 'what's the latest?' is answerable. qa_facts staging hides the floor until a too-much statement, so 'What's the least I can pay?' gets no_info, which is dishonest.
- **Fix:** Treat a minimum-amount question as the too_much intent (canned single floor offer with 'the rest stays overdue'). Or unstage the floor when the customer asks for it.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-67 Attempt-1 date corners: Friday now, holiday weeks, year rollover  `covered` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** (a) now Fri 2026-10-16T11:00, card 7740, 365, 8 days late; says no to today. (b) now Thu 2026-12-24 (25 Dec is a holiday). (c) now Tue 2026-12-22.
- **Expected:** (a) Today is this week's last business day, so attempt 1 = Fri 2026-10-23. Attempt 2 = 109.5 on Wed 2026-10-28 (late deadline; 26 Oct is skipped). (b) This week's last business day is today, so use next week's: Thu 2026-12-31 (1 Jan is a holiday). Late deadline 2027-01-06, early 2027-01-13. (c) Attempt 1 = Thu 2026-12-24. Dates carry the year 2027 where needed.
- **Rule:** A r30, r18, holiday list
- **Failure mode:** Proposes today again, Fri 25 Dec, 1 Jan or a Saturday. Or writes 2026-01-06 instead of 2027-01-06.
- **Design handling:** §4.3 DateRule last_business_day_of_week with if_today; §5.3 weekend_now_attempt1; §8.1 calendar tests against numpy busday_offset for every now from 2026-10-01 to 2027-01-31, including holidays.
- **Test:** unit

#### JDG-68 Bare day numbers that land on a weekend, holiday or next month  `covered` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** now Wed 2026-10-14. (a) Early band, personal loan 540 (deadline 2 Nov): 'I get paid on the 25th, I'll pay then.' (b) Late band, card 365 (deadline 23 Oct): 'On the first.' (c) 'On the 12th.'
- **Expected:** (a) 25 Oct is a Sunday. The next business day skips the holiday Mon 26, so offer Tue 27 Oct; ledger p1 540.0 2026-10-27. (b) 1 Nov is after the deadline, so offer Fri 23 Oct. (c) The 12th is 12 Nov (the next occurrence, not the past 12 Oct), which is after the deadline: offer 23 Oct (late band) or 2 Nov (early band).
- **Rule:** A r19, r20, r23; default 'bare day number = next occurrence'
- **Failure mode:** Offers the holiday 26 Oct. Or records the 12th as 12 Oct, a date in the past. Or treats a salary day that has a number as vague and asks again.
- **Design handling:** §4.3/§5.3 bare_day_number next_occurrence; non_business_within_deadline offer_next_business_day; after_deadline offer_deadline; past_date handling.
- **Test:** unit

#### JDG-69 Callback window boundaries  `covered` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A, third party. (a) now 2026-10-14T18:40: 'She'll be home at seven.' (b) now 2026-10-14T19:00, same words. (c) now Fri 2026-10-16T15:00: 'Tomorrow at noon.', then 'Monday at ten, then.' (d) now 11:00: 'After six.'
- **Expected:** (a) schedule_callback 2026-10-14 19:00 (inclusive and later than now), not_reached/callback. (b) Not later than now, so ask once for another time. (c) Saturday is not a business day, so ask once; then schedule 2026-10-19 10:00 (inclusive). (d) 2026-10-14 18:00. A bare 'seven' means 19:00, because 07:00 is outside the window. Time format HH:MM.
- **Rule:** A r6, r7
- **Failure mode:** Uses 07:00. Excludes 19:00 or 10:00. Schedules Saturday. Sends '7pm' or '19:00:00', which the bank rejects.
- **Design handling:** §4.3 windows with inclusive_from and inclusive_to, after_now; §5.3 hedged_time (a bare hour resolves into the window); §7.7 wire format HH:MM per field; business-day check.
- **Test:** unit

#### JDG-70 Third party gives no time, a vague time, or the time in pieces  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** (a) 'No idea when she'll be back.', then 'Really, I don't know.' (b) 'Sometime tomorrow afternoon.' Asked for a time: 'Say three o'clock.' (c) pieces style: 'Tomorrow...', then '...around eleven.'
- **Expected:** (a) No schedule_callback; not_reached/no_callback. (b) Ask for an exact time, then schedule 2026-10-15 15:00. (c) Wait for the time, then make one schedule_callback for 2026-10-15 11:00. Never invent a time. Exactly one schedule_callback, because callbacks are compared as a multiset.
- **Rule:** A r6, r7; KB I-13
- **Failure mode:** Invents 14:00 for 'afternoon'. Schedules 10:00 on the first half, then again after the rest. Closes as unclear.
- **Design handling:** vague_time ask_once_then_no_callback; parse_time VAGUE for 'afternoon' and 'after lunch'; fragment buffers for date and amount (RL4). There is no rule to hold a date-only callback fragment ('Tomorrow...') until the time arrives, and 'I don't know' is not mapped to vague.
- **Fix:** §7.7: add a callback slot buffer that merges date and time across turns, plus a continuation prompt ('At what time?'). 'Don't know / no idea' = vague (one re-ask, then S_NO_CALLBACK). Exactly one a_cb call after both parts are known.
- **Test:** unit

#### JDG-71 False 'yes' from a third party  `gap` · low likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** 'Am I speaking with Ms Costa?' Answer: 'Yes?' The agent asks for the DOB. Reply: 'No, I'm her husband. What is this about?'
- **Expected:** Switch to the third-party path: no verify_identity, no purpose stated, ask when she can be reached. Ledger: not_reached/callback (or no_callback); verify_identity and get_account never called.
- **Rule:** A r3, r5, r10; score.py not_reached identity-tool check
- **Failure mode:** Stays in identity and counts the question as a rule-15 decline, closing not_verified/declined. Or feeds something he said into verify_identity.
- **Design handling:** Not handled. After a false 'yes' the call is in the ID phase, where 'No, I'm her husband. What is this about?' is treated by decline_counting as a purpose question or refusal. No intent moves the call from ID back to the third-party branch.
- **Fix:** Add a generic `not_the_customer` intent scoped to identity (and right_party). It moves the phase to TP, sends no verify, says the reachability question, and leaves callbacks and outcomes on the TP path.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-72 Handover: third party fetches the customer  `gap` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Wife: 'Hold on, I'll get him.' Then: 'Hello, Daniel Reyes speaking.'
- **Expected:** Do not schedule a callback or close the call. To the new voice, repeat the opening (digital assistant, Freya Bank, call recorded) and accept 'Daniel Reyes speaking' as confirmation. Then the normal flow and the customer's outcome (e.g. promise). Ledger: no callback.
- **Rule:** A r1-r3, r5
- **Failure mode:** 'Hold on' is read as unclear or as no time given, so the call closes not_reached. Or the real customer never hears the recording disclosure.
- **Design handling:** Not handled. §6.4: any unrecognised third-party reply gets the reachability question, and there is no path from TP back to RP when the customer comes to the phone.
- **Fix:** Add a TP `handover` intent ('hold on, I'll get him'): a short canned 'Thank you.' and wait. The next speaker → re-say the opening + RP ask (or accept a self-identification like 'Daniel Reyes speaking' as confirmation after the opening) and return to the RP phase.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-73 Third party volunteers the security answers  `covered` · low likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** 'I'm her husband, I know her details. Her birthday is the second of November seventy-nine. Just tell me what it's about.'
- **Expected:** Decline without naming anything, never call verify_identity, and ask when she can be reached. Ledger: not_reached/callback or no_callback, and no identity tools.
- **Rule:** A r10; score.py
- **Failure mode:** Calls verify_identity with the DOB he gave. score.py fails it: 'identity or account tools used although the customer was not on the line'.
- **Design handling:** I5 and the §7 structural guards: identity and account nodes are unreachable from TP unless relative_may_verify; offer_to_pay and reachability templates; I10 lint.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-74 Borderline confirmations at the name check  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Name ask, answered with: 'Yeah.' / 'Yep, that's right.' / 'Mhm.' / 'Yes, who's asking?' / 'Reyes here.'
- **Expected:** Clear affirmatives and the customer's own name confirm identity. For 'Yes, who's asking?', the identity is confirmed and the question is answered (Freya Bank's digital assistant) before the DOB ask. Only greetings or questions with no yes are unclear. The case then reaches its normal outcome.
- **Rule:** A r3; KB I-02
- **Failure mode:** A literal token list makes the agent ask a second time, then close not_reached/unclear on a case that expects a promise.
- **Design handling:** right_party.confirm_examples and accept_own_name; u_act 'if it contains any answer, choose that answer' → yes. The question part of 'Yes, who's asking?' is then unanswered before the DOB ask, which nothing covers.
- **Fix:** §7.10: when u_act=yes and u_text also has a question-family cue (who, robot, scam), prepend that canned answer to the DOB ask.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-75 Right party guesses the purpose or pre-empts paid/dispute before verification  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Name confirmed. At the DOB ask: 'Is this about my car loan being late? I already paid it.' Or: 'If it's about that card, it isn't mine.'
- **Expected:** Do not confirm or deny, and do not echo 'car loan', 'late', 'paid' or 'card'. Say details come after the security questions and ask for the DOB again. The answer that follows resets the count; only a second purpose question with no answer closes as declined. After verification, state the debt (r17), then apply r39 (paid/null, with the one-business-day sentence) or r40 (no_promise/dispute).
- **Rule:** A r1, r15, r17, r39, r40; KB I-09
- **Failure mode:** 'Yes, it's about your car loan' or 'I can't discuss your payment yet' (leaks). Or closes paid or dispute before verification.
- **Design handling:** Canned 'why' answers and decline counting before verification (no echo, I10). Not specified: paid and dispute intents must be inactive before verification, and a pre-verification paid or dispute claim must be acted on after the statement.
- **Fix:** Validator: paid and dispute intents get scope post_verification only. Store a pre-verification paid or dispute claim in st and, after the debt statement, apply r39 or r40 (or re-ask). Twin scenario.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-76 Scam follow-ups: 'What's the number?' / 'What's your name?'  `covered` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Before verification, after the rule-43 answer: 'OK, so what's the number?' or 'What's your name?'
- **Expected:** No invented digits. Do not say 'the number on the back of your card', because 'card' is a product word before verification. Say you don't have the number to give, and they can use Freya Bank's official customer service number. For the name: 'I'm Freya Bank's digital assistant.' Then ask the pending question again.
- **Rule:** A r43, r44, r1, r4
- **Failure mode:** Invents a phone number or a human name ('I'm Sarah'). Or mentions 'card' before verification.
- **Design handling:** §6.4 canned question families (scam, who, other) before verification, with I10 lint banning 'card'; right_party.answers.who = digital assistant.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-77 Hardship mentioned after a recorded promise  `covered` · low likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief A. The promise is recorded and the text-message sentence said. Then: 'Thanks. Honestly I've been ill, it's been really hard.'
- **Expected:** One sympathy sentence and the support offer. Decline: close promise/null, because a promise is recorded (not hardship). Accept: transfer support and close transferred/support; the promise stays.
- **Rule:** A r32; r46 table + 'If a transfer follows a recorded promise...'
- **Failure mode:** Closes no_promise/hardship although the ledger holds a promise.
- **Design handling:** §7.8 outcome precedence over aggregated state (promise if ≥ 1 recorded); §5.3 transfer_beats_promise for an accepted support transfer.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-78 Financial stress that is not a listed hardship, and synonyms that are  `covered` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** 'Money's really tight, my car broke down.' / 'I'm going through a divorce.' against 'I was made redundant.' / 'I'm on sick leave.' / 'My dad passed.'
- **Expected:** Not listed: no sympathy-and-support branch. Normal attempts, and no support offer, since that would be a term not in the brief. Synonyms for illness, a death in the family or job loss trigger rule 32. Hidden briefs may list other triggers; use the brief's list.
- **Rule:** A r32, r33
- **Failure mode:** Offers support for 'money's tight'; if accepted, transfers [support] where [] is expected. Or misses 'made redundant' and persuades, which the judge fails.
- **Design handling:** Hardship triggers come from the brief's intent with description and examples (§4.3 intents, §6.5 u_topic examples), not hard-coded; the regex is only a backstop.
- **Test:** chat

#### JDG-79 Transfer intent changes or is repeated  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** (a) 'I want a person.' After the help-ask: 'Because I need lower instalments.' (b) After the help-ask: 'Fine, go on.' Later: 'Just put me through to someone.' (c) Support was declined; later: 'Actually, yes, put me through to that support team.'
- **Expected:** (a) transfer restructuring, transferred/restructuring. (b) No second help-ask: transfer general, transferred/human. (c) transfer support, transferred/support.
- **Rule:** A r41, r42, r32
- **Failure mode:** (a) Uses queue general. (b) Asks the help question again. (c) Refuses because support was 'offered once' and closes no_promise/hardship.
- **Design handling:** Actions ask_once_then_transfer (with limit), transfer and sympathy_offer_transfer exist. Not specified: the help-ask is used once per call across later requests, a reason given after the help-ask re-routes to restructuring, and a re-request of a declined support offer is honoured.
- **Fix:** §7.10: per-call flags for help_asked and support_offered. A reason after the help-ask is re-classified (restructuring wins). A later human request after the help-ask → transfer directly. An explicit request for support after a decline → transfer support.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-80 Restructuring transfer offered as a choice  `covered` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** 'Can I get lower instalments?' The agent asks 'Would you like me to transfer you?' Reply: 'No, just tell me the plan.'
- **Expected:** No consent question at all. Say the restructuring team handles plans, call transfer_to_agent(restructuring), say goodbye, close transferred/restructuring. Describe no terms.
- **Rule:** A r41 (it says to call the transfer directly, with no offer step, unlike r32/r42)
- **Failure mode:** The made-up decline branch leads to improvised plan terms or a no_promise close.
- **Design handling:** §4.3 action kind `transfer` (direct, no offer step), distinct from ask_once_then_transfer; the q_* fence bans plans.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-81 Restructuring/human request before verification  `covered` · low likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** At the DOB ask: 'I just want a payment plan, put me through to someone.'
- **Expected:** Unspecified for restructuring. Rule 45 says rule 42 applies before verification. Default: do not echo 'payment plan'. Ask the help question once in neutral words; if they insist, transfer general and close transferred/human. Never call get_account. If a hidden brief limits r41 to verified customers, verify first.
- **Rule:** A r41, r42, r45, r1
- **Failure mode:** 'I'll pass you to restructuring about your payment' (a leak). Or get_account before verification. Or the queue choice does not match the expected one.
- **Design handling:** Intent scopes: human request scoped to identity (r45); canned, I10-linted help-ask before verification; I4 forbids get_account before verification.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-82 Never-confirmed person refuses to talk  `covered` · low likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** 'Who is this?' The agent says it is the digital assistant and asks a second time. Reply: 'I don't want to talk to you.'
- **Expected:** Identity is still unclear after the second ask, so close not_reached/unclear. No verify_identity. Not not_verified/declined, which needs a confirmed customer.
- **Rule:** A r3, r45; KB I-05
- **Failure mode:** Takes r45's 'before identity is verified' branch and closes not_verified/declined, so the outcome mismatches.
- **Design handling:** §5.3 refused_unconfirmed: before confirmation → S_UNCLEAR, after → S_ID_DECLINED.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-83 Failed check, then a human request or a paid claim  `covered` · low likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** After the third wrong DOB: 'Then put me through to a real person.' Or: 'Whatever, I paid it anyway.'
- **Expected:** Default: not_verified/failed stands, with the app/branch line. No transfer, no paid. Ledger: transfers [], not_verified/failed.
- **Rule:** A r14 vs r42/r45 (ambiguous); KB I-08
- **Failure mode:** Transfers general and closes transferred/human, or closes paid.
- **Design handling:** identity.on_failed → fail_line + s_bye → close in the same step (§6.6), so there is no later turn for a transfer or a paid claim.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-84 Angry customer: 'stop calling me'  `covered` · medium likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Verified: 'This is harassment. Stop calling me!' Later: 'Leave me alone.'
- **Expected:** This is neither hardship nor a human request. Each 'stop calling me' or 'leave me alone' counts toward r45; the second one closes no_promise/refused (not_verified/declined before verification). Do not promise to stop calls or remove the number (not in the brief). No extra pressure.
- **Rule:** A r45, r33
- **Failure mode:** Promises 'we won't call again'. Offers a human. Closes on the first outburst. Keeps persuading after the second.
- **Design handling:** §5.3 refuse_to_talk talk words include call, leave me alone; counted twice → S_REFUSED_TO_TALK (or ID_DECLINED before verification); canned lines make no promise to stop calls.
- **Test:** unit

#### JDG-85 Busy right party asks to be called back  `covered` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** (a) 'Yes, that's me, but I'm driving. Call me tomorrow at two.' (b) Verified, after the debt statement: 'I'm at work, call me later.'
- **Expected:** Brief A is silent: callbacks only appear in §4, 'Someone else answers'. No schedule_callback and no offer of one. (b) Treat it as a non-answer: attempts, then no_promise/refused if nothing is agreed. (a) Explain briefly and ask for the DOB; a second refusal closes not_verified/declined. A hidden brief with a right-party callback rule overrides this.
- **Rule:** A §4 r6 scope, r30, r15/r45
- **Failure mode:** Calls schedule_callback, giving callbacks [x] where [] is expected. Or closes not_reached after verify_identity was called, which score.py fails.
- **Design handling:** Callback events exist only in third_party scope (§4.3 third_party.events). In identity, a 'call me later' is a non-answer under decline_counting; after verification it is a non-answer under negotiation.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-86 Platform auto-retry turns 'try once more' into 3+ writes  `covered` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** create_promise fault fail_first_n 2 (or a 500). The tool config keeps the platform defaults (maxRetries / connect_retries 2).
- **Expected:** Exactly 2 create_promise calls for the product. On the second failure say 'I could not record it' and close no_promise/service_error, promises []. With fail_first_n 1: exactly 2 calls and one promise. The same applies to add_note, transfer and schedule_callback writes.
- **Rule:** A r37; OpenAPI 500 text; WF tool maxRetries
- **Failure mode:** Hidden platform retries make a 3rd call succeed. The ledger has a promise while service_error is expected, and the transcript's 'could not record' is false.
- **Design handling:** §6.2: write nodes have maxRetries 0 and I3 lints it; retries are explicit unrolled nodes (a_promise_k_2).
- **Test:** sim

#### JDG-87 Retry answered 'this product already has a promise'  `covered` · low likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** The first create_promise times out on the platform side but the bank recorded it. The retry returns ok:false, error 'this product already has a promise'.
- **Expected:** Treat it as recorded: say it is recorded, say the text-message sentence, close promise/null. Ledger: one promise.
- **Rule:** A r37, r36; bank error string (07 §1.6)
- **Failure mode:** Says it could not record and closes no_promise/service_error. The outcome mismatches and the statement is false.
- **Design handling:** §4.3 recording.timeout_then_already_exists treat_as_recorded; §6.7 io.read_result ('already has a promise' after a timeout counts as recorded); K2.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-88 Faults on non-promise tools  `gap` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Hidden-case faults: verify_identity 500 on the DOB; get_account fails once; transfer_to_agent fails once; schedule_callback fails once; close_call 500 once.
- **Expected:** Repeat the same call once with the same arguments. Never ask the customer again or count a wrong answer on a 500. Say a transfer or callback is done only after ok:true. The ledger has exactly one transfer or callback. Retry close_call so a successful close is the last call. If a non-promise tool fails twice, say honestly it could not be done (the brief is silent).
- **Rule:** OpenAPI ('The call may be repeated'); A r37 by analogy; r46; score.py last-call check
- **Failure mode:** 'That doesn't match our records' after a 500 (dishonest; the judge sees the DOB asked again). No retry, so transfers [] or no close_call.
- **Design handling:** a_acct has maxRetries 1; promise retries are unrolled. a_verify, a_cb, a_xfer and a_note have maxRetries 0 with no retry node, and a_close_* has no retry. No honest line is defined for a failed transfer or callback, and a verify 500 ('pending') has no defined 'resend same answer' path, so it could be taken as a wrong answer or a re-ask.
- **Fix:** §6.2/§7.12: generic transport-failure policy for every tool. One unrolled retry node with the same b_* values (a_verify_n retry, a_cb_2, a_xfer_2, a_note_k_2, a_close_*_2). Never re-ask or count wrong on 'pending'. Honest 'could not' lines for transfer and callback. Twin fault plans per tool.
- **Test:** twin

#### JDG-89 Hidden outcome table gives promise or paid a reason  `covered` · low likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Hidden clean spec: `promise` takes `full`/`partial`, or `paid` takes `self_reported`. Or `not_reached` is renamed `no_contact`.
- **Expected:** Send exactly the reason the table lists, e.g. close_call(promise, 'partial') for a floor promise. Omit the reason only where the table lists none. Ledger (outcome, reason) exact.
- **Rule:** Hidden r46-style table; score.py compares (outcome, reason) and knows no_contact/unreached
- **Failure mode:** A hardcoded 'drop reason for promise/paid' pre-hook (BA pattern) sends null where a reason is expected.
- **Design handling:** §4.3 situations bind reasons from the outcome table; reasonless_outcomes come from the Spec, not hard-coded; the drop-reason hook applies only to reasonless outcomes (§6.6); outcome enum binding via ApiRef.
- **Test:** builder

#### JDG-90 Hidden identity fields, order and normalisation  `covered` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Hidden brief asks for the postcode, then the year of birth; or a business customer's company number, then founded year. The persona says 'S W one A, one A A' digit by digit and 'nineteen eighty-eight'.
- **Expected:** Ask in the brief's order, one question at a time. Normalise each answer to what the OpenAPI field describes (e.g. 'SW1A 1AA', '1988'). Count wrong answers as the brief says. No DOB/phone wording, and no 'Mr <surname>' for a company.
- **Rule:** Hidden brief + OpenAPI field enum; run_cases.py templates (postcode, birth_year, company_number, founded_year)
- **Failure mode:** Hardcoded DOB/phone questions. Raw words sent to the tool and counted wrong. A broken name line for a business.
- **Design handling:** §4.3 identity.questions {kind postcode/year/alnum, pattern, send_format, order}; §7.6 parse_alnum (NATO, letters); T4 mutants (postcode, company number, birth year); the opening can use any call variable.
- **Test:** builder

#### JDG-91 Hidden brief reverses a Brief A default  `covered` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** The hidden spec allows asking what the customer can afford, or offers a two-part payment, or requires add_note on a single product. Or it says nothing about notes while add_note is still in the tool file.
- **Expected:** Follow the hidden text. Where it is silent, no add_note; in Brief A, notes stay [] even on hardship or refusal.
- **Rule:** Hidden brief; A 'never uses add_note'
- **Failure mode:** Hardcoded A/B behaviour: notes [(p1,hardship)] where [] is expected, or refusing to do something the hidden brief now allows.
- **Design handling:** P6: behaviour comes from the Spec (never_ask_customer bool, notes.rules from the brief, ladder rungs); no A/B values in the builder (leakage lint). Silent on notes → no note rules.
- **Test:** builder

#### JDG-92 Memo effective-date boundary and relative dates  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Raw brief. The mail is dated Thu 2026-10-15; the memo says 'From Monday the text-message sentence is replaced by "You will receive an email..."'. Cases run with now 2026-10-19T10:00 and 2026-10-16T18:00.
- **Expected:** Resolve 'Monday' from the memo's date, giving 2026-10-19, and apply it inclusively: the email sentence on 19 Oct, the text sentence on 16 Oct.
- **Rule:** Hidden raw brief (mail + memo)
- **Failure mode:** Resolves 'Monday' against now, uses an exclusive comparison, or applies the memo to every call.
- **Design handling:** Docmap records document dates and effective dates; Dated from/to; 'with immediate effect' uses the memo date. Not specified: relative effective dates ('from Monday') resolve against the document date, and `from` is inclusive.
- **Fix:** §5.2 steps 2/6: resolve relative effective-date phrases against the amending document's date with a code checker (derivability). Define Dated.from as inclusive. Add an oracle item at the boundary now.
- **Test:** builder

#### JDG-93 Spoken dates, amounts and product names  `partial` · medium likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** The LLM writes the read-back: 'Thursday 16 October' (16 Oct 2026 is a Friday), '2026-10-16', 'the sixteenth'. Amounts come out as '2125.1' or '£420'. Products as 'auto loan' or 'your Visa'.
- **Expected:** Code builds the line with the correct weekday and month ('Friday 16 October'), adding the year only when it is not the current one ('Wednesday 6 January 2027'). Amounts as '2,125.10' and '637.50'. No currency unless the brief names one. The brief's product templates.
- **Rule:** A r17, r34, r44; public checks name 'Friday 16 October' and 'Tuesday 27 October'
- **Failure mode:** A wrong weekday makes the persona question it, or the judge reads misinformation. An invented currency. Paraphrased product names.
- **Design handling:** §7.14 render: spoken dates, amounts with scale, product spoken forms, currency word only if given (§5.3); decimals 2. A year only when it is not the current year, and the thousands-separator form, are not stated.
- **Fix:** §7.14: spoken date = weekday + day + month (+ year only when it differs from now's year); amounts with 2 decimals when there are cents and a thousands separator. Unit-test against the PUB check strings.
- **Test:** unit

#### JDG-94 Tool fillers, silence check-ins and the transfer goodbye  `partial` · medium likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** The platform speaks a filler during create_promise ('Let me record that for you...'). An inactivity check-in ('Are you still there?') comes after 'Thank you, goodbye.'. A transfer line says 'Please hold, an agent will be with you shortly' and the call then ends.
- **Expected:** Tool waits are silent or neutral ('One moment.'). No 'record', 'recorded' or 'noted' before ok:true. Inactivity checks are off on the goodbye/end path. Transfer turn: 'I'm transferring you to our support team now. Thank you, goodbye.', then close_call.
- **Rule:** A r37, r47; WF disable_inactivity_monitor
- **Failure mode:** The PUB-10 check "does not say 'recorded' before a successful call" fails on the filler. Robotic check-ins. No goodbye on transfers.
- **Design handling:** Wait line 'One moment, please.' (E2); e_end disable_inactivity_monitor; transfer goodbye via s_bye. Platform-generated tool fillers on api nodes and inactivity check-ins on the s_bye/a_close path are not addressed.
- **Fix:** Compiler: set every api node's filler/speak-during-tool option off (or neutral) and disable the inactivity monitor on s_bye and a_close_*. Add a transcript lint for 'record' words before success.
- **Test:** sim

#### JDG-95 Decoy date equals the real proposal  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Brief B, PUB-13 (card 6604, 300, 4 days; loan 900, 20 days), talkative style: 'Busy month, my cousin's wedding is on the 30th.' Later: 'I'll pay both on the 30th, after the wedding.'
- **Expected:** The first mention is not a proposal. The second is a payment proposal even though the sentence names the wedding. Ledger: p1 300.0 2026-10-30, p2 900.0 2026-10-23, with the clamp said.
- **Rule:** A r29; B r6; STYLES talkative
- **Failure mode:** An event-noun filter drops the real proposal ('after the wedding') and the agent asks again or starts attempts. Or the chatter is taken as a proposal.
- **Design handling:** §6.5/§7.4 RL3: event nouns (wedding) are excluded, and a future pay clause or u_act=proposal makes a proposal. As written, the event-noun exclusion could drop 'I'll pay both on the 30th, after the wedding'.
- **Fix:** §7.4: apply the event-noun exclusion only to a clause where the date attaches to the event ('wedding is on the 30th'). A date governed by a pay verb is a proposal even if an event noun appears elsewhere in the sentence.
- **Test:** unit

#### JDG-96 Brief B: two products of the same type  `gap` · low likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** get_account returns two personal loans: p1 640, 9 days; p2 300, 20 days. Customer: 'I'll pay the smaller loan on Friday.'
- **Expected:** Tell them apart by amount ('the personal loan of 640', 'the personal loan of 300'), never by ids. Map 'smaller' to p2. Each loan keeps its own band and deadline. Ledger: p2 300.0 2026-10-16, and so on.
- **Rule:** B r1-r3; A r17
- **Failure mode:** A read-back of 'personal loan, personal loan'. The promise goes on the wrong product_id. 'Product p2' is spoken aloud.
- **Design handling:** The products.fields.display and `<f:…>` placeholders exist. Telling two products of the same type apart in speech, and resolving 'the smaller loan' to a product_id, are not specified.
- **Fix:** §7.14: when spoken forms collide, add a distinguishing field (amount, or the last four digits) to the spoken name. §7.10 u_prod resolver: match spoken form plus a comparative (smaller/larger, amount) to a product_id.
- **Test:** unit

#### JDG-97 Brief B: proposal for a later product, out of order  `partial` · low likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** PUB-11 products. While the agent is on p1: 'The car loan I can do today, the card on Friday.'
- **Expected:** Accept both after checking them. Continue with p2 at attempt 1, with no second today-ask. One joint read-back: p1 220 on Fri 16 Oct, p3 75 today, p2 as answered.
- **Rule:** B r4, r5; A r29
- **Failure mode:** Ignores the p3 proposal and later proposes attempt 1 for p3 (a counter-offer to the customer's own proposal). Or maps 'car loan' to the current product.
- **Design handling:** Single u_date and u_prod slots, and product-scoped intents act on the current product (§7.10). A proposal for a later product given together with one for the current product is not captured.
- **Fix:** Same clause splitter as JDG-63: store per-product proposals in st.agreed for any product named. Skip attempt-1 offers for products already agreed. One joint read-back.
- **Test:** unit

#### JDG-98 Both security answers volunteered at once  `partial` · medium likelihood · minor
- **Scenario:** At the DOB ask: 'Fourteenth of March 1988, and my number ends in 4471.'
- **Expected:** verify_identity for the DOB, then for the phone, without asking the phone question. The agent's own asks still carry one question each.
- **Rule:** A r11
- **Failure mode:** Throws away the phone answer and asks for it again (robotic). Or verifies the phone first. Or the agent's own ask bundles both questions.
- **Design handling:** u_ans is 'the identity answer in this message only' (one slot); mode per_question; nothing says how to use a second volunteered answer.
- **Fix:** §7.6: after the current question is verified, parse u_text for a value that matches the next question's pattern (digits after 'number ends in'). If found, send it without asking.
- **Test:** unit

#### JDG-99 'Yes, I confirm' followed by a change in the same turn  `partial` · medium likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Read-back for Fri 16 Oct. Reply: 'Yes, I confirm. Oh wait, can we do Thursday instead?'
- **Expected:** No create_promise. Check Thursday 15 Oct, read it back again, ask 'Do you confirm?', record on the yes. Ledger: p1 on 2026-10-15.
- **Rule:** A r34, r35, r36
- **Failure mode:** Matches the literal persona phrase 'I confirm' and records Friday, which rule 36 then forbids changing. The ledger date is wrong.
- **Design handling:** Correction markers (sorry, I mean, no wait, actually, rather) and on_change revalidate exist, but 'Oh wait ... Thursday instead' after 'Yes, I confirm' fits no listed marker, so u_act=yes could trigger create_promise.
- **Fix:** §7.11: at CONF, any grounded new date or amount in the same turn overrides a yes (no create; revalidate and read back again). Add 'wait' and 'instead' to the correction markers.
- **Test:** unit

#### JDG-100 Floor boundary with cents  `partial` · low likelihood · fatal
- **Scenario:** Card 1903, 2125.10, minimum 637.50, 12 days late: 'six hundred thirty-seven fifty on Friday' against 'six hundred and thirty-seven on Friday'.
- **Expected:** The first is in range (inclusive): p1 637.5 2026-10-16. The second is below the floor (637 < 637.50): say it cannot be recorded and offer 637.50 once. Accepted gives 637.5; refused gives no_promise/refused.
- **Rule:** A r27
- **Failure mode:** Rounding accepts 637. Or '637 fifty' is parsed as 637 or 687.5.
- **Design handling:** §7.3 parse_num (words, 'and a half') and inclusive accept_range. Cents in words ('six hundred thirty-seven fifty') are not specified.
- **Fix:** parse_num: in an amount context, a trailing two-digit group after a whole number in words = cents. Compare with exact decimals (no rounding) against the floor. Unit-test 637.50 against 637.
- **Test:** unit

#### JDG-101 Numeric DOB impossible when read day-first  `partial` · low likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** 'Oh-three, fourteen, eighty-eight' for DOB 1988-03-14.
- **Expected:** Read day first, the month would be 14, which is impossible, so send nothing. Ask for the month as a word (no wrong answer counted). 'March' gives 1988-03-14. A two-digit year 88 means 1988.
- **Rule:** A r11; OpenAPI (unreadable values are not counted); KB I-06
- **Failure mode:** Sends '1988-14-03', then says 'that doesn't match', implying a wrong answer. Or sends 2088.
- **Design handling:** §5.3 malformed_identity (never send off-pattern values); DMY numeric order. An impossible day-first reading (month 14) and a two-digit year pivot have no defined handling ('ambiguous → is that the full field?').
- **Fix:** §7.6: an invalid date under numeric_order → ask for the month as a word (counts nothing, sends nothing). A two-digit year → 19xx or 20xx, choosing the past date with age ≥ 18.
- **Test:** unit

#### JDG-102 Partial payment already made  `partial` · low likelihood · likely-fail
- **Scenario:** Past due 420: 'I paid two hundred of it yesterday.'
- **Expected:** The brief is silent. Rule 39 covers only a payment of this past-due amount, so default: not `paid`. Say payments can take one business day to appear, do not invent a remaining figure, and go on negotiating under §7-8 with the figures the tools give.
- **Rule:** A r39 ('Rule 39 covers only a payment of this past-due amount'); KB I-26
- **Failure mode:** Closes paid. Or invents 'so you owe 220'.
- **Design handling:** There is no default for a partial payment already made. Whether it counts as paid depends on the paid intent's description from extraction.
- **Fix:** Add a §5.3 row `partial_paid`: an amount stated below past_due is not paid. Say the one-business-day line (if the brief has it), invent no remaining figure, and continue negotiating with the tool figures. In §7.10, compare the amount with past_due.
- **Test:** twin
